zh: 正徘徊瞻顾，不知何以为计时，突然眼前一亮，那个在吃“门板饭”的，一定是了。杭州的饭店，犹有两宋的遗风，楼上雅坐，楼下卖各样熟食，卸下排门当案板，摆满了朱漆大盘，盛着现成菜肴，另有长条凳，横置案前，贩夫走卒，杂然并坐，称为吃“门板饭”。一碗饭盛来，象座塔似地堆得老高，不是吃惯了的，无法下箸，不知从顶上吃起，还是从中腰吃起？所以那些“穿短打”的一见这位“寄大衫儿的”落座，都不免注目，一则是觉得衣冠中人来吃“门板饭”，事所罕见，二则是要看他如何吃法？不会吃，“塔尖”会倒下来，大家在等着看他的笑话。
en: As Gao hesitated, looking this way and that and wondering what to do, he suddenly spotted the man. The fellow eating at the improvised counter must be him. Hangzhou's eating houses still preserved customs from the Song dynasties. Upstairs were comfortable private seats; downstairs, cooked dishes were sold from large red-lacquered platters laid out on doors taken from their frames and used as counters. Long benches stood in front, where pedlars and labourers sat together for what was called a “door-plank meal.” A bowl of rice arrived heaped as high as a little pagoda. Anyone unused to it hardly knew where to put his chopsticks: should he begin at the summit or halfway down? The men in short working clothes therefore stared when this customer in a long gown sat down. A gentleman dining in such a place was unusual enough; more than that, they wanted to see how he would manage the rice. If he did not know the trick, the top would collapse. They were waiting for the joke.

zh: 就在这时，高升已经赶到，侧面端详，十有八九不错，便冒叫一声：“胡少爷！”
en: Gao had reached him by then. Studying his profile, he felt almost certain and ventured a call: “Young Master Hu!”

zh: 这一声叫，那班“穿短打的”都笑了，哪有少爷来吃门板饭的？
en: The men in working clothes laughed. What young master would come here for a door-plank meal?

zh: 高升到杭州虽不久，对这些情形已大致明白，自己也觉得“胡少爷”叫得不妥，真的是他，他也不便答应，于是走到他身边问道，“请问，贵姓可是胡？”
en: Though new to Hangzhou, Gao had already learned something of local ways. He realised that his form of address was ill chosen. Even if this was Hu, he might be embarrassed to answer. Gao therefore approached and asked, “Excuse me, is your surname Hu?”

zh: “不错。怎地？”
en: “Yes. What of it?”

zh: “台甫可是上雪下岩？”
en: “And is your courtesy name Xueyan?”

zh: 正是胡雪岩，他把刚拈起的竹箸放下，问道：“我是胡雪岩。从未见过尊驾……”
en: It was indeed Hu Xueyan. Setting down the bamboo chopsticks he had just picked up, he said, “I am Hu Xueyan, but I don't believe we've met...”

zh: 高升看他衣服黯旧，于思满面，知道这位“胡少爷”落魄了，才去吃门板饭。如果当街相认传出去是件新闻，对自己老爷的官声，不大好听，所以此时不肯说破王有龄的姓名，只说：“敝上姓王，一见就知道。胡少爷不必在这里吃饭了，我陪了你去看敝上。”
en: His faded clothes and unshaven face told Gao that Young Master Hu had fallen on hard times, which explained his choice of eating place. A public reunion in the street would make a story, and might not sound well for his master's official reputation. He therefore avoided naming Wang Youling. “My master's surname is Wang. You'll know him as soon as you see him. There's no need to eat here, Young Master Hu. Let me take you to him.”

zh: 说罢不问青红皂白，一手摸一把铜钱放在案板上，一手便去搀扶胡雪岩，跨出条凳，接着便招一招手，唤来一顶待雇的小轿。
en: Without waiting for an answer, he put a handful of copper coins on the counter with one hand and helped Hu step over the bench with the other. Then he beckoned to a small hired sedan chair waiting nearby.

zh: 胡雪岩有些摸不着头脑，不肯上轿，拉住高升问道：“贵上是哪一位？”
en: Hu was bewildered and refused to get in. Catching Gao's arm, he asked, “Which Mr Wang is your master?”

zh: “是……”高升放低了声音说：“我家老爷的官印，上有下龄。”
en: “He is...” Gao lowered his voice. “His official name is Youling.”

zh: “啊！”胡雪岩顿时眼睛发亮：“是他。现在在哪里？”
en: “Ah!” Hu's eyes lit up. “It's him! Where is he now?”

zh: “公馆在清和坊。胡少爷请上轿。”
en: “His residence is in Qinghefang. Please get into the chair.”

zh: 等他上了轿，高升说明地址，等小轿一抬走，他又赶了去见王有龄，略略说明经过。王有龄欢喜无量，也上了蓝呢大轿，催轿班快走。
en: Once Hu was seated, Gao gave the bearers the address. As soon as the little chair moved away, he hurried back to Wang and briefly explained what had happened. Wang was overjoyed. He too climbed into his blue-cloth chair and urged the bearers to hurry.

zh: 一前一后，几乎同时抬到王家，高升先一步赶到，叫人开了中门，两顶轿子，一起抬到厅前。彼此下轿相见，都有疑在梦中的感觉，尤其是王有龄，看到胡雪岩穷途末路的神情，鼻子发酸，双眼发热。
en: The two chairs reached the Wang residence almost together. Gao had run ahead and ordered the central gates opened, so both were carried straight to the hall. When the friends stepped out and faced each other, each felt as though he were dreaming. Wang in particular was overwhelmed by the sight of Hu's poverty and desperation. His nose stung and his eyes grew hot.

zh: “雪岩！”
en: “Xueyan!”

zh: “雪轩！”
en: “Xuexuan!”

zh: 两个人这样招呼过，却又没有话了，彼此都有无数话梗塞在喉头，还有无数话积压在心头，但嘴只有一张，不知先说哪一句好？
en: After those greetings, neither could speak. Countless things crowded their throats and weighed upon their hearts, but with only one mouth apiece, neither knew what to say first.

zh: 一旁的高升不能不开口了：“请老爷陪着胡少爷到客厅坐！”
en: Gao, standing beside them, had to intervene. “Perhaps Your Honour would take Young Master Hu into the reception room.”

zh: “啊！”王有龄这才省悟，“来，来！雪岩且先坐下歇一歇再说。也不必在外面了，请到后面去，舒服些。”
en: “Ah!” Wang came to himself. “Come, Xueyan. Sit down and rest before we talk. We needn't stay out here. Let's go to the back, where it's more comfortable.”

zh: 一引引到后堂，躲在屏风后面张望的王太太，慌忙回避。胡雪岩瞥见裙幅飘动，也有些踌躇。这下又提醒了王有龄。
en: He led Hu into the rear hall. Mrs Wang, who had been watching from behind a screen, hurried away. Catching sight of her moving skirt, Hu hesitated. This reminded Wang of something else.

zh: “太太！”他高声喊道，“见见我这位兄弟！”
en: “My dear!” he called loudly. “Come and meet this brother of mine.”

zh: 这样的交情，比通家之好更进一层，真个如手足一样，王太太便很大方地走了出来，含着笑，指着胡雪岩，却望着她丈夫问：“这位就是你日思夜梦的胡少爷了！”
en: Their bond went beyond ordinary family friendship; they were truly like brothers. Mrs Wang therefore came out without embarrassment. Smiling, she pointed to Hu but spoke to her husband. “So this is the Young Master Hu you've been thinking of by day and dreaming of by night!”

zh: “不敢当这个称呼！”胡雪岩一躬到地。
en: “I hardly deserve that title.” Hu bowed deeply.

zh: 王太太还了礼，很感动地说：“胡少爷！真正不知怎么感激你？雪轩一回杭州，就去看你，扑个空回来，长吁短叹，不知如何是好？我埋怨雪轩，这么好的朋友，哪有不请教人家府上在哪里的道理？如今好了，是在哪里遇见的？”
en: She returned the bow and spoke with feeling. “Young Master Hu, we really don't know how to thank you. As soon as Xuexuan came back to Hangzhou, he went to look for you. He returned without finding you and sighed and fretted, not knowing what to do. I blamed him: how could anyone have so good a friend without asking where he lived? Now all is well. Where did you meet?”

zh: “在，在路上。”胡雪岩有些窘。
en: “In... in the street.” Hu looked embarrassed.

zh: 王存龄的由意外凉喜所引起的激动，这时已稍稍平伏，催着他妻子说：“太太！我们的话，三天三夜说不完，你此刻先别问，我们都还没有吃饭，看看，有现成的，先端几个碟子来喝酒。”
en: Wang's first rush of emotion had subsided a little. He hurried his wife along. “My dear, we couldn't finish all we have to say in three days and nights. Leave the questions for now. Neither of us has eaten. See what is ready and bring a few dishes so we can have a drink.”

zh: “有，有。”王太太笑着答道，“请胡少爷上书房去吧，那里清静。”
en: “Certainly.” She smiled. “Take Young Master Hu to the study. It's quiet there.”

zh: “对了！”
en: “Just so!”

zh: 王有龄又把胡雪岩引到书房，接着王太太便带着丫头、老妈子，亲来照料。胡雪岩享受着这一份人情温暖，顿觉这大半年来的飘泊无依之苦，受得也还值得。
en: Wang led Hu to the study. His wife soon followed with the maid and older servant to look after them herself. Surrounded by such warmth, Hu felt that even the hardship and insecurity of the past half-year had been worth enduring.

zh: “雪轩！”他问，“你几时回来的？”
en: “Xuexuan,” he asked, “when did you return?”

zh: “回来还不到一个月。”王有龄对自己心满意足，但看到胡雪岩却有些伤心，“雪岩，你怎么弄成这样子？”
en: “Less than a month ago.” Wang was thoroughly content with his own circumstances, but the sight of Hu saddened him. “Xueyan, how did you come to this?”

zh: “说来话长。”胡雪岩欲言又止地，“你呢？我看很得意？”
en: “It's a long story.” Hu hesitated. “What about you? You seem to have done very well.”

zh: “那还不是靠你。连番奇遇，什么《今古奇观》上的‘倒运汉巧遇洞庭红’，比起我来，都算不了什么！”王有龄略停一停，大声又说，“好了！反正只要找到了你就好办了。来，来，今天不醉不休。“
en: “And whom have I to thank but you? I've had one extraordinary encounter after another. That tale in Strange Stories Old and New about the unlucky man whose fortune turns through Dongting oranges is nothing beside my experience.” He paused, then exclaimed, “Well, now that I've found you, everything can be put right. Come! Today we drink until we're drunk.”

zh: 另一面方桌上已摆下四个碟子，两副杯筷，等他们坐下，王太太亲自用块手中，裹着一把酒壶来替他们斟酒。胡雪岩便慌忙逊谢。
en: Four dishes and two sets of cups and chopsticks had been laid on a square table nearby. When they sat down, Mrs Wang wrapped a cloth around the wine pot and poured for them herself. Hu hurriedly protested at the honour.

zh: “太太！”王有龄说，“你敬了兄弟的酒，就请到厨房里去吧，免得兄弟多礼，反而拘束。”
en: “My dear,” Wang said, “drink a toast to my brother, then go and attend to the kitchen. Otherwise he'll feel obliged to keep standing on ceremony and won't be at ease.”

zh: 于是王太太向胡雪岩敬过酒，退了出去，留下一个丫头侍候。
en: She toasted Hu and withdrew, leaving a maid to serve them.

zh: 于是一面吃，一面说，王有龄自通州遇见何桂清开始，一直谈到奉委海运局坐办，其间也补叙了他自己的家世。所以这一席话谈得酒都凉了。
en: As they ate, Wang told his story, from meeting He Guiqing in Tongzhou to his appointment at the Sea Transport Bureau, filling in his own family background along the way. By the time he finished, the wine had gone cold.

zh: “恭喜，恭喜！”胡雪岩此时已喝得满面红光，那副倒霉相消失得无形无踪，很得意地笑道：“还是我的眼光不错，看出你到了脱运交运的当儿，果不其然。”
en: “Congratulations!” Hu's face was flushed with drink, and every trace of his defeated appearance had vanished. He smiled proudly. “My judgement was right after all. I could see that your bad luck was ending and your good fortune about to begin. And so it did.”

zh: “交运也者，是遇见了你。雪岩，”王有龄愧歉不安地说，“无怪乎内人说我湖涂，受你的大恩，竟连府上在哪里都不知道。今天，你可得好好儿跟我说一说了。”
en: “My good fortune began when I met you.” Wang looked ashamed. “Xueyan, no wonder my wife calls me muddle-headed. You did me such an immense kindness, yet I never even learned where you lived. Today you must tell me all about yourself.”

zh: “自然要跟你说。”胡雪岩喝口酒，大马金刀地把双手撑在桌角，微偏着头问他：“雪轩，你看我是何等样人？”
en: “Of course I shall.” Hu drank, planted both hands squarely on the corners of the table, and tilted his head slightly. “Xuexuan, what sort of man do you take me for?”

zh: 王有龄看他的气度，再想一想以前茶店里所得的印象，认为他必是个官宦人家的了弟，但不免有些甘于下流，所以不好好读书，成天在茶店里厮混。
en: Considering his manner and recalling his earlier impressions in the teahouse, Wang supposed that Hu must be the son of an official family, but one who had lowered his ambitions and preferred idling in teahouses to serious study.

zh: 当然，这“甘于下流”四字，他是不能出口的，便这样答道：“兄弟，我说句话，你别生气。我看你象个纨袴.”
en: Naturally, he could not voice that judgement so bluntly. “Brother, don't be offended,” he said. “I took you for a well-born young idler.”

zh: “纨袴？”胡雪岩笑了，“你倒不说我是‘撩鬼儿’！”这是杭州话，地痞无赖叫“撩鬼儿”。
en: “An idler?” Hu laughed. “You might have called me a liaogui'er instead!” That was the Hangzhou expression for a street loafer or local ruffian.

zh: “那我就猜不到了。请你实说了吧，我心里急得很！”
en: “Then I can't guess. Tell me the truth. I'm terribly anxious to know.”

zh: “那就告诉你，我在钱庄里‘学生意’……”
en: “Very well. I learned my trade in a private bank...”

zh: 胡雪岩父死家贫，从小就在钱庄里当学徒，杭州人称为“学生子”，从扫地倒溺壶开始，由于他绝顶聪明，善于识人，而且能言善道，手面大方，所以三年满师，立刻便成了那家钱庄一名得力的伙计，起先是“立柜台”，以后获得东家和“大伙”的信任，派出去收帐，从来不曾出过纰漏。
en: Hu's father had died, leaving the family poor, and he had entered a private bank as an apprentice while still a boy. In Hangzhou, such apprentices were called “trade students.” He began with sweeping floors and emptying chamber pots. But he was extraordinarily quick, a shrewd judge of people, persuasive in speech, and generous in his dealings. When his three-year apprenticeship ended, he immediately became one of the bank's most useful employees. At first he worked at the counter. Later, having won the confidence of both proprietor and manager, he was sent out to collect debts. He had never made a mistake.

zh: 前一年夏天跟王有龄攀谈，知道他是一名候补盐大使，打算着想北上“投供”、加捐时，胡雪岩刚有笔款子可收。这笔款子正好五百两，原是吃了“倒帐”的，在钱庄来说，已经认赔出帐，如果能够收到，完全是意外收入。
en: The previous summer, when he learned from Wang that he held a salt-station superintendent's qualification and wanted to go north to register and purchase a higher one, Hu happened to have a debt to collect. It was exactly five hundred taels. The account had gone bad, and the bank had already accepted the loss and written it off. Any recovery would be an unexpected gain.

zh: 但是，这笔钱在别人收不到，欠债的人有个绿营的营官撑腰，他要不还，钱庄怕麻烦，也不敢惹他。不过此人跟胡雪岩很谈得来，不知怎么发了笔财，让胡雪岩打听到了去找他，他表示别人来不行，胡雪岩来另当别论，很慷慨地约期归清。
en: No one else could collect it. The debtor had the backing of a Green Standard officer, and if he refused to pay, the bank preferred to avoid trouble rather than challenge him. But he and Hu got on well. Hu heard that the man had somehow come into money and went to see him. The debtor said that anyone else would have been refused, but Hu was a different matter. He readily fixed a date to settle the debt in full.

zh: 胡雪岩一念怜才，决定拉王有龄一把。他想，反正这笔款子在钱庄已经无法收回，如今转借了给王有龄，将来能还最好，不能还，钱庄也没有损失。
en: Moved by sympathy for Wang's wasted abilities, Hu decided to help him. Since the bank had already treated the money as irrecoverable, he reasoned, he could lend it on to Wang. If Wang repaid it later, all the better. If not, the bank would be no worse off than before.

zh: 这个想法也不能说没有道理，悄悄儿做了，人不知，鬼不觉，一时也不会有人去查问这件事。坏就坏在他和盘托出，而且自己写了一张王有龄出面的借据送到总管店务的“大伙”那里。
en: There was a certain logic in the argument. Had he acted quietly, nobody would have known, and nobody would have thought to inquire for some time. The trouble was that he disclosed everything. He even drew up a promissory note in Wang's name and delivered it to the manager responsible for the bank's business.

zh: “大伙”受东家的委托，如何能容胡雪岩这种“一厢情愿”的想法，念在他平日有功，也不追保，请他卷了铺盖。这一下在同行中传了出去，都说他胆大妄为，现在幸亏是五百两，如果是五千两、五万两，他也这样擅作主张，岂不把一爿店都弄“倒灶”了？
en: Entrusted with the proprietor's affairs, how could the manager accept such unilateral reasoning? In view of Hu's past service, he did not pursue Hu's guarantor, but he told him to pack his bedding and leave. Word spread through the trade. Everyone said Hu was recklessly presumptuous. Luckily, this had been only five hundred taels. What if it had been five thousand or fifty thousand? If he took such liberties, might he not ruin an entire firm?

zh: 为了这个名声在外，同业间虽知他是一把好手，却谁也不敢用他。同时又有人怀疑他平日好赌，或许是在赌博上失利，无以为计，饰词挪用了这笔款子。这个恶名一传，生路就越加困难了。
en: With that reputation, no bank would employ him, although everyone knew his abilities. Some also suspected that, given his fondness for gambling, he had lost money and invented the story to cover its misappropriation. Once this further accusation spread, earning a living became harder still.

zh: “谢天谢地，”胡雪岩讲到这里，如释重负似地说，“你总算回来了！不管那笔款子怎么样，以你现在的身分，先可以把我的不白之冤，洗刷干净。“
en: “Thank heaven you've finally returned,” Hu said, as though relieved of a heavy burden. “Whatever happens about the money, your present position will at least enable me to clear my name.”

zh: 润湿的双眼的王有龄，长长叹了口气：“唉，如果你我没有今天的相遇，谁会想得到我冥冥中已经害得你好惨。如今，大恩不言谢，你看我该怎么办？”
en: With moist eyes, Wang sighed deeply. “If we hadn't met again today, who would have imagined that I had unknowingly caused you so much suffering? Such kindness is beyond thanks. Tell me what I should do.”

zh: “这要看你。我如何能说？”
en: “That's for you to decide. How can I say?”

zh: “不，不！”王有龄发觉自己措词不妥，赶紧抢着说道，“我不是这意思，我是说，你的事就是我的事。怎么样把面子十足挣回来，这我有办法，现在要问你的是，你今后作何打算？是不是想回原来的那家钱庄？”
en: “No, no!” Realising that he had expressed himself badly, Wang hurried to explain. “That's not what I mean. Your affairs are mine. I know how to restore your reputation fully. What I want to ask is what you intend to do next. Would you like to return to the bank?”

zh: 胡雪岩摇摇头，说了句杭州的俗语：“ ‘回汤豆腐干’，没有味道了。”
en: Hu shook his head and quoted a Hangzhou saying: “Dried bean curd put back in the broth has lost its flavour.”

zh: “那么，是想自立门户？”
en: “Then do you want to set up on your own?”

zh: 这句话说到了他心里，但就在要开口承认时，忽然转念，开一家钱庄不是轻而易举的事，要本钱也要有人照应。王有龄现在刚刚得了个差使，力量还有限，如果自己承认有此念头，看他做人极讲义气，为了感恩图报，一定想尽办法来帮自己，千斤重担挑不动而非挑不可，那就先要把他自己压坏。
en: That was exactly what Hu wanted. But as he was about to admit it, another thought stopped him. Opening a bank was no simple matter. It required capital and powerful support. Wang had only just obtained an appointment; his resources were still limited. If Hu declared his ambition, Wang's loyalty and gratitude would compel him to do everything possible to help. He would take on a burden too heavy for him and be crushed beneath it.

zh: 这怎么可以？
en: How could Hu allow that?

zh: 有些警惕，胡雪岩便改口了，“我不想再吃钱庄饭。”他说，“你局里用的人大概不少，随便替我寻个吃闲饭的差使好了。”
en: Alarmed by the possibility, he changed his answer. “I don't want to earn my living in banking any more. Your bureau must employ quite a few people. Just find me some easy post where I can draw a salary without much work.”

zh: 王有龄欣悦地笑了，学着杭州话说：“闲饭是没有得把你吃的。”
en: Wang smiled happily and imitated the Hangzhou accent. “There'll be no money for sitting idle!”

zh: 胡雪岩心里明白，他会在海运局里给他安排一个重要职司，到那时候，好好拿些本事来帮一帮他。把他帮发达了，再跟他借几千两银子出来做本钱，那就受之无愧了。
en: Hu understood. Wang would give him an important position at the bureau. Then he could use his abilities to help his friend. Once Wang had prospered through that help, Hu could borrow a few thousand taels as capital with a clear conscience.

zh: 吃得酒醉饭饱，沏上两碗上好的龙井茶，赓续未尽的谈兴，王有龄提到黄宗汉的为人，把椿寿一案，当作新闻来讲，又提到黄抚台难伺候，然后话锋一转，接上今日上院谒见的情形。
en: When they had eaten and drunk their fill, two bowls of excellent Longjing tea were brought in, and the conversation continued. Wang described Huang's character, recounted Chunshou's case as news, and spoke of the governor's difficult temper. From there, he turned to the audience he had attended that day.

zh: “那么你现在预备怎么样呢？”胡雪岩问，意思是问他如何能够把应运的漕米，尽速运到上海，交兑足额？
en: “What do you intend to do now?” Hu asked. He meant how Wang would get the outstanding grain to Shanghai quickly enough to complete delivery.

zh: “我有什么办法？只有尽力去催。”
en: “What can I do? Only press them as hard as possible.”

zh: “难！”胡雪岩摇着头说，“你们做官的。哪晓得人家的苦楚？一改海运，漕丁都没饭吃了，所以老实说一句，漕帮巴不得此事不成！你们想从运河运米到上海，你急他不急，慢慢儿拖你过限期，你就知道他的厉害了。”
en: “That's difficult.” Hu shook his head. “You officials have no idea what other people suffer. Once transport shifts to the sea, the canal boatmen lose their livelihood. To speak frankly, the associations would be delighted if the scheme failed. You want them to carry the rice to Shanghai by canal. You're in a hurry; they aren't. They'll drag things out until you miss the deadline. Then you'll discover how much power they have.”

zh: “啊！”工有龄矍然而起，“照你这一说，是非逾限不可了。那怎么办呢？”
en: “Ah!” Wang sat bolt upright. “Then we're certain to miss it. What can be done?”

zh: “总有办法好想。”胡雪岩敲敲自己的太阳穴说，“世上没有没有办法的事，只怕不用脑筋。我就有一个办法，这个办法包你省事，不过要多花几两银子，保住了抚台的红顶子，这几两银子也值。”
en: “There's always a way.” Hu tapped his temple. “Nothing in the world is beyond a solution; the difficulty is getting people to think. I have a plan that will save you a great deal of trouble. It'll cost a little extra, but that's money well spent if it saves the governor's rank.”

zh: 王有龄有些不大相信，但不妨听他讲了再说，便点点头：“看看你是什么好办法？”
en: Wang was doubtful, but might as well hear him out. He nodded. “Let's hear this excellent plan of yours.”

zh: “米总是米，到哪里都一样。缺多少就地补充，我的意思是，在上海买了米，交兑足额，不就没事了吗？”
en: “Rice is rice, wherever it comes from. Make up the shortage where it's needed. Buy rice in Shanghai, deliver the full quota, and the problem is solved.”

zh: 他的话还没有完，王有龄已经高兴得跳了起来：“妙极，妙极！准定这么办。”
en: Before he had finished, Wang sprang up in delight. “Excellent! Excellent! That's what we'll do.”

zh: “不过有一层，风声千万不可泄漏。漕米不是少数，风声一漏出去，米商立刻扳价，差额太大，事情也难办。”
en: “But there's one condition: not a word must leak out. This is a large quantity of rice. If the merchants hear of it, they'll immediately raise their prices. Too great a difference, and the business becomes difficult.”

zh: “是的。”王有龄定定神盘算了一会，问道，“雪岩，你有没有功名？”
en: “Yes.” Wang collected himself and considered the matter. “Xueyan, do you hold any official or scholarly qualification?”

zh: “我是一品老百姓。”
en: “I'm a commoner of the first rank.”

zh: “应该去报个捐，哪怕是‘未入流’，总算也是个官，办事就方便了。现在我只好下个‘关书’……“王有龄又踌躇着说，”也还不知道能不能聘你当‘文案’？“
en: “You ought to purchase a title. Even one below the regular ranks would make you an official of sorts and simplify your work. For now, I can only issue a letter of engagement...” Wang hesitated. “And I'm not even sure whether I can appoint you as a secretary.”

zh: “慢慢来，慢慢来！”胡雪岩怕他为难，赶紧安慰着他说。
en: “One thing at a time,” Hu said quickly, anxious not to embarrass him.

zh: “怎么能慢呢？我要请你帮我的忙，总得有个名义才好。”王有龄皱着眉说，“头绪太多，也只好一样一样来。雪岩，你府上还有什么人？”
en: “How can it wait? If you're to help me, you need some recognised position.” Wang frowned. “There are too many loose ends. I suppose we must deal with them one by one. Xueyan, who is there in your family?”

zh: “一个娘，一个老婆。”
en: “My mother and my wife.”

zh: “那我要去拜见老伯母……”
en: “Then I must pay my respects to your mother...”

zh: “不必，不必！”胡雪岩急忙拦阻，“目前不必。我住的那条巷，轿子部抬不进去的，舍下也没有个坐处，你现在来不是替我增光，倒是出我的丑。将来再说。“
en: “No, no!” Hu hastily stopped him. “Not just now. The lane where I live is too narrow for a sedan chair, and there's nowhere fit to sit inside. A visit now would expose my poverty rather than do me honour. Another time.”

zh: 王有龄知道他说的是老实话，便不再提此事，站起身来说：“你先坐一坐，我就来。”
en: Knowing that Hu meant it, Wang let the matter drop. He rose. “Sit here a moment. I'll be back.”

zh: 等他回出来时，手里拿着五十两一张银票，只说先拿着用。胡雪岩也不客气，收了下来，起身告辞，说明天再来。
en: When he returned, he held a bank draft for fifty taels and simply told Hu to use it for the present. Hu accepted without ceremony, rose to leave, and promised to return the next day.

zh: “今天就不留你了。明天一早，请你到我局里，我专诚等你？还有一件，你把府上的地址留下来。”
en: “I won't keep you today. Come to the bureau first thing tomorrow; I'll be waiting especially for you. And one more thing: leave me your address.”

zh: 胡雪岩住在元宝街，把详细地址留了下来。王有龄随后便吩咐高开，备办四色精致礼物，用“世愚侄”的名帖，到元宝街去替“胡老太太”请安。
en: Hu lived in Yuanbao Street and supplied the details. Wang then ordered Gao to prepare four kinds of carefully chosen gifts and take them there to pay his respects to Madam Hu, with a card identifying himself humbly as her nephew by family friendship.

zh: 高升送了礼回来，十分高兴，因为胡雪岩虽然境况不佳，出手极其大方，封了四两银子的赏号。
en: Gao returned from delivering the presents in high spirits. Poor as Hu was, he remained remarkably open-handed and had given Gao a gratuity of four taels.

zh: “我不肯收，赏得太多了。”高升报告主人，“胡少爷非叫我收不可，他说他亦是慷他人之慨。”
en: “I tried to refuse; it was far too much,” Gao told his master. “But Young Master Hu insisted. He said he was only being generous with someone else's money.”

zh: “那你就收下好了。”王有龄心里在想，照胡雪岩的才干和脾气，一旦有了机会，发达起来极快，自己的前程，怕与此人的关系极大，倒要好好用一用他。
en: “Then you should accept it.” Wang thought that, with Hu's ability and temperament, any opportunity would lead him rapidly to success. His own future might depend greatly on this man. He must make good use of him.

zh: 第二天一早，胡雪岩应约而至，穿得极其华丽。高升早已奉命在等候，一见他来，直接领到“签押房”，王有龄便问：“那家钱庄在哪里？”
en: Early the next morning Hu arrived as promised, splendidly dressed. Gao, already instructed to wait for him, took him straight to Wang's private office. Wang asked, “Where is that bank?”

zh: “在‘下城’盐桥。字号叫做‘信和’。”
en: “In the Lower City, at Salt Bridge. It's called Xinhe.”

zh: “请你陪我去。你是原经手，那张笔据上是怎么写的？请你先告诉我，免得话接不上头。”
en: “Come with me. You handled the original transaction, so tell me how the note was worded. I don't want my account to contradict it.”

zh: 胡雪岩想了一下，徐徐念道：“立笔据人候补盐大使王有龄，兹因进京投供正用，凭中胡雪岩向信和钱庄借到库平足纹五百两整。言明两年内归清，照市行息。口说无凭，特立笔据存照。”
en: Hu reflected, then recited slowly: “I, Wang Youling, expectant salt-station superintendent, acknowledge borrowing from Xinhe Bank, through the intermediary Hu Xueyan, five hundred taels of full-standard silver by the treasury weight, for necessary expenses in travelling to the capital to register. Repayment is agreed within two years, with interest at the prevailing market rate. Since a verbal statement is insufficient proof, this note is issued as a record.”

zh: “那么，该当多少利息呢？”
en: “How much interest would that make?”

zh: “这要看银根松紧，并无一定。”胡雪岩说，“多则一分二，少则七厘，统算打它一分，十个月的工夫，五十两银子的利息也就差不多了。”
en: “It depends on the availability of money; there is no fixed rate,” Hu said. “At the high end, one point two per cent a month; at the low end, seven-tenths. If we take one per cent throughout, ten months would make about fifty taels.”

zh: 于是王有龄写了一张“支公费六百两”的条谕，叫高升拿到帐房。不一会管帐的司事，亲自带人捧了银子来，刚从藩库里领来的，一百一锭的官宝六锭，出炉以后，还未用过，簇簇光新，令人耀眼。
en: Wang wrote an order authorising an advance of six hundred taels against official expenses and sent Gao to the accounts office. Soon the accounts clerk came himself with men carrying the silver: six official ingots, each weighing a hundred taels, newly received from the provincial treasury. Fresh from the mould and never used, they gleamed brilliantly.

zh: “走吧？一起到信和去。”
en: “Shall we go to Xinhe together?”

zh: “这样，我不必去了。”胡雪岩说，“我一去了，那里的‘大伙’，当着我的面，不免难为情。再有一句话，请你捧信和两句，也不必说穿，我们已见过面。”
en: “In that case, I'd better stay here,” Hu replied. “If I go, the manager will be embarrassed in front of me. There's something else: say a few good words about Xinhe, and don't mention that we've already met.”

zh: 王有龄听他这一说，对胡雪岩又有了深一层的认识，此人居心仁厚，至少手段漂亮，换了另一个人，象这样可以扬眉吐气的机会，岂肯轻易放弃？
en: This deepened Wang's understanding of his friend. Hu was generous-hearted—or at the very least, remarkably graceful in his methods. Who else would willingly surrender such a chance to hold his head high before those who had dismissed him?

zh: 而他居然愿意委屈自己，保全别人的面子，好宽的度量！
en: Yet Hu was prepared to deny himself that satisfaction in order to preserve another man's dignity. What breadth of mind!

zh: 因为如此，王有龄原来预备穿了公服，鸣锣喝道去唬信和一下的，这时也改了主意，换上便衣，坐一顶小轿，把六锭银子，用个布包袱一包，放在轿内，带着高升，悄悄来到了信和。
en: For that reason, Wang abandoned his own plan to put on formal robes and arrive with gongs and shouted commands to frighten the bank. Instead, he changed into ordinary clothes, took a small chair, wrapped the six ingots in a cloth bundle, placed them inside, and went quietly to Xinhe with Gao.

zh: 轿子一停，高升先去投帖。钱庄对官场的消息最灵通，信和的大伙张胖子，一看名帖，知道是抚台面前的红人，王有龄三字也似乎听说，细想一想，恍然记起，却急出一身汗！没奈何，且接了进来再说。
en: As soon as the chair stopped, Gao went ahead with the visiting card. Banks were exceptionally well informed about official affairs. Xinhe's manager, known as Fat Zhang, recognised the name of a man favoured by the governor. The name Wang Youling also sounded familiar in another connection. A moment's thought brought the memory back—and broke him into a sweat. There was nothing to do but receive the visitor and see what happened.

zh: 等他走到门口，王有龄已经下轿，张胖子当门先请了个安，迎到客堂，忙着招呼，泡茶拿水烟袋，肃客上坐，然后陪笑问道，“王大老爷光降小号，不知有何吩咐？”
en: By the time Zhang reached the entrance, Wang had stepped out of his chair. Zhang saluted, welcomed him into the reception room, and busied himself with tea, a water pipe, and the seat of honour. Smiling deferentially, he asked, “To what do we owe the honour of your visit? What instructions may we carry out?”

zh: 王有龄摘下墨晶大眼镜，从容答道：“宝号有位姓胡的朋友，请出来一见。”
en: Wang removed his dark spectacles and answered calmly, “You have a man here surnamed Hu. Please ask him to come and see me.”

zh: “喔，喔，是说胡雪岩？他不在小号了。王大老爷有事，吩咐我也一样。”
en: “Oh, you mean Hu Xueyan? He is no longer with us. Whatever Your Honour requires, you may tell me instead.”

zh: 王有龄停了停说：“还没有请教贵姓？”
en: After a pause, Wang said, “May I ask your surname?”

zh: “不敢！敝姓张，都叫我张胖子，我受敝东的委托，信和大小事体都能做三分主。”
en: “Zhang, sir. Everyone calls me Fat Zhang. My employer has entrusted me with the business, so I have some authority in all the firm's affairs.”

zh: “好！”王有龄向高升说道：“把银子拿了出来！”接着转脸向张胖子：“去年承宝号放给我的款子，我今天来料理一下。”
en: “Good.” Wang turned to Gao. “Bring in the silver.” Then he addressed Zhang again. “Your bank kindly lent me money last year. I've come to settle the matter.”

zh: “不忙，不忙！王大老爷尽管放着用。”
en: “There's no hurry at all. Please keep it for your use.”

zh: “那不好！有借有还，再借不难。我也知道宝号资本雄厚，信誉卓著，不在乎这笔放款。不过，在我总是早还早了。不必客气，请把本利算一算，顺便把原笔据取出来。
en: “That would hardly do. Repay one loan, and another can be obtained when needed. I know your firm has ample capital and an excellent reputation, and that this sum is of little concern to you. But I would prefer to settle it sooner rather than later. Please calculate the principal and interest and bring out the original note.”

zh: 张胖子刚才急出一身汗，就因为取不来原笔据，那张笔据，当时当它无用，不知弄到什么地方去了。
en: It was precisely the thought of that note that had made Zhang sweat. He could not produce it. Having regarded it as worthless, he no longer knew where it had gone.

zh: 做钱庄这行生意，交往的都是官员绅士、富商大贾，全靠应酬的手段灵活，张胖子的机变极快，他在想，反正拿不出笔据，便收不回欠款，这件事解铃还须系铃人，要把小胡找到，才有圆满解决的希望，此时落得放漂亮些。
en: A banker dealt with officials, gentry, and wealthy merchants, and depended upon flexibility in social dealings. Zhang thought quickly. Without the note, he could hardly collect the debt. The man who had tied the knot must untie it: only by finding Hu could he hope for a satisfactory solution. For now, he might as well appear generous.

zh: 因此，他先深深一揖，奉上一顶高帽子：“王大老爷真正是第一等的仁德君子！象你老这样菩萨样的主客，小号请都请不到，哪里好把财神爷推出门？尊款准定放着，几时等雪岩来了再说。倒是王大老爷局里有款子汇划，小号与上海南市‘三大’——大亨、大豫、大丰都有往来，这三家与‘沙船帮’极熟，漕米海运的运费，由小号划到‘三大，去付，极其方便，汇水亦决不敢多要。王大老爷何不让小号效劳？”
en: He bowed deeply and offered extravagant praise. “Your Honour is a gentleman of the highest benevolence. A client as kind as you is a blessing our little firm could scarcely hope for. How could we turn the God of Wealth away? Please keep the money until Xueyan returns. Meanwhile, if your bureau needs remittance services, we have dealings with the Big Three in Shanghai's southern city: Daheng, Dayu, and Dafeng. They know the sand-junk association extremely well. Freight payments for the sea grain shipments could be remitted through us to them with the greatest convenience, and our charges would be very modest. Why not allow us to serve you?”

zh: 这是他不明内情，海运运费不归浙江直接付给船商，但也不必跟他说破。
en: He did not understand the arrangements: Zhejiang did not pay the shipowners directly for sea freight. But Wang saw no need to explain that.

zh: 王有龄依然要还那五百两的欠款，张胖子便再三不肯，推来推去，他只好说了一半实话。
en: He continued to insist on repaying the five hundred taels. Zhang repeatedly refused, until the exchange finally drove him to tell half the truth.

zh: “老实禀告王大老爷，这笔款子放出，可以说是万无一失，所以笔据不笔据，无关紧要，也不知放到哪里去了？改天寻着了再来领。至于利息，根本不在话下，钱庄盘利钱，也要看看人，王大老爷以后照顾小号的地方多的是，这点利息再要算，教敝东家晓得了，一定会怪我。”
en: “To be frank, Your Honour, we considered the loan absolutely secure, so the note itself hardly mattered. I don't know where it was put. Once we find it, we can come to collect. As for interest, that needn't be mentioned. A bank considers who its customer is when calculating interest. Your Honour will have many opportunities to favour us in future. If I charged you this little sum, my employer would certainly blame me.”

zh: 话说得够漂亮，王有龄因为体谅胡雪岩的心意，决定做得比便更漂亮，便叫高升把包袱解开，取了五百五十两银子，堆在桌上，然后从容说道，“承情已多，岂好不算利息？当时我也听那位姓胡的朋友说过，利息多则一分二，少则七厘，看银根松紧而定，现在我们通扯一分，十个月工夫，我送子金五十两，这里一共五百五十两，你请收了，随便写个本利还清的笔据给我，原来我所出的那张借据，寻着了便烦你销毁了它。宝号做生意真是能为客户打算，佩服之至。我局里公款甚多，那位姓胡的朋友来了，你请他来谈一谈，我跟宝号做个长期往来。”
en: The speech was handsome enough. Remembering Hu's wishes, Wang decided to be more gracious still. He had Gao unwrap the bundle and lay five hundred and fifty taels on the table. Then he said calmly, “I am already much indebted to you. How could I refuse to pay interest? Your Mr Hu told me that the rate varied with the money market, from seven-tenths to one point two per cent a month. Let us take one per cent throughout. For ten months, that makes fifty taels. Here are five hundred and fifty in all. Please accept them and give me a simple receipt stating that principal and interest are paid in full. When you find my original note, kindly destroy it. I admire the consideration your firm shows its clients. My bureau handles substantial public funds. When Mr Hu returns, ask him to come and discuss a lasting business relationship between us.”

zh: 张胖子喜出望外，当时写了还清的笔据，交与高升收执，一面决不肯收利息，但王有龄非要给不可，也就只好不断道谢着收了下来。
en: Overjoyed, Zhang immediately wrote a receipt and gave it to Gao. He still protested against taking interest, but Wang insisted, leaving him only to accept with repeated thanks.

zh: 等他恭送上轿，王有龄觉得这件事做得十分痛快有趣，暗中匿笑，这张胖子想做海运局的生意，一走马上派人去找胡雪岩。谁知胡雪岩已经打定主意，不会回他店里，现在让他吃个空心汤圆，白欢喜一场，也算是对他叫胡雪岩卷铺盖的小小惩罚。
en: After Zhang had respectfully seen him into his chair, Wang felt that the whole affair had been both satisfying and amusing. He smiled inwardly. Eager for the bureau's business, Zhang would send someone to find Hu as soon as he left. Little did he know that Hu had already decided never to return to the bank. Letting him enjoy an empty promise for a while was a small punishment for having dismissed Hu.

zh: 回到局里，会着胡雪岩说了经过。胡雪岩怕信和派人到家去找，戳穿真相，那时却之不可，不免麻烦，所以匆匆赶回家去，预作安排。王有龄也换了公服，上院去谒见黄抚台，还怕他不见，特为告诉刘二，说是为漕米交兑一案，有了极好的办法，要见抚台面禀一切。
en: Back at the bureau, Wang told Hu what had happened. Hu feared that Xinhe might send someone to his home and discover the truth, making refusal awkward. He hurried back to prepare for that possibility. Wang changed into official robes and went to see the governor. Afraid of being denied an audience, he specifically told Liu Er that he had found an excellent solution to the grain-delivery problem and wished to explain it in person.

zh: 刘二因为他交了去的两张“条子”，王有龄都已有了适当的安插，自然见他的情，所以到了里面，格外替他说好话。黄宗汉一听“有了极好的办法”，立刻接见，而且脸色也大不相同了。
en: Liu was grateful that Wang had suitably placed both men whose cards he had submitted. He therefore spoke especially well of him inside. At the words “an excellent solution,” Huang granted an immediate audience, and his expression was entirely changed.

zh: 等把胡雪岩想出来的移花接木之计一说，黄宗汉大为兴奋，不过不能当时就作决定，因为兹事体大。
en: When Wang explained Hu's scheme of substitution, Huang became very excited. But the matter was too important for an immediate decision.

zh: 于是黄宗汉派“戈什哈”把藩司和督粮道都请了来，在抚署西花厅秘密商议。为了早日交代公事，大家都赞成王有龄所提出来的办法，但也不是没有顾虑。
en: He sent attendants to summon the provincial treasurer and grain intendant for a secret consultation in the western reception room. Eager to complete the official business, all supported Wang's proposal, though not without reservations.

zh: “漕米悉数运到上海，早已出奏有案。如今忽然在上海买米垫补，倘或叫那位‘都老爷’知道了，开上一个玩笑……”麟桂迟疑了一下说，“那倒真不是开玩笑的事！”
en: “We have already reported to the throne that all the grain has reached Shanghai,” Lingui said. “If we now buy rice there to make up the shortage, and that censor gets wind of it and decides to have a little fun...” He hesitated. “It would be no laughing matter.”

zh: “藩台的话说得是。”督粮道接口附和，然后瞥了王有龄一眼，自语似他说，“能有个人挡一下就好了。”
en: “The treasurer is right,” the grain intendant agreed. Glancing at Wang, he added as though speaking to himself, “It would help if someone could stand in front of the affair.”

zh: 所谓“挡一下”，就是有人出面去做，上头装作不知道，一旦出了来，有个躲闪斡旋的余地。抚、藩两宪都明白他的意思，但这个可以来“挡一下”的人在哪里呢？
en: He meant that someone should handle it openly while the senior officials professed ignorance. If it came to light, they would have room to evade responsibility or negotiate a way out. Both governor and treasurer understood. But who would put himself in that position?

zh: 黄宗仪和麟桂都把眼光飘了过来，王有龄便毫不考虑地说：“我蒙宪台大人栽培，既然承乏海运，责无旁贷，可否交给我去料理？”
en: Their eyes drifted towards Wang. Without hesitation, he said, “I owe my advancement to Your Excellencies. Having been entrusted with sea transport, I cannot evade the responsibility. May the matter be left to me?”

zh: 在座三上司立刻都表示了嘉许之意，黄宗汉慢吞吞说道：“漕米是天庚正供，且当军兴之际，粮食为兵营之命脉，不能不从权办理。既然有龄兄勇于任事，你们就在这里好好谈一谈吧！”说完，他站起身来，向里走去。
en: All three superiors immediately showed their approval. Huang spoke slowly. “The grain tax supplies the imperial storehouses. In wartime, provisions are the army's lifeblood, and expedient measures cannot be avoided. Since Brother Youling is willing to assume responsibility, you may discuss the details here.” With that, he rose and withdrew to the inner rooms.

zh: 抚合似乎置身事外了，麟桂因为有椿寿的前车之鉴，凡事以预留卸责的地步力宗旨。倒是督粮道有担当，很用心地与王有龄商定了处置的细节。
en: The governor appeared to have removed himself from the business. Mindful of Chunshou's fate, Lingui too aimed above all to leave himself a way to disclaim responsibility. The grain intendant, however, showed some willingness to act and worked carefully with Wang on the details.

zh: 这里面的关键是，要在上海找个大粮商，先垫出一批糙米，交给江苏藩司倪良耀，然后等浙江的漕米运到上海归垫。换句说话，是要那粮商先卖出，后买进，当然，买进卖出价钱上有差额，米的成色也不同，漕米的成色极坏，需要贴补差价，另外再加盘运的损耗，这笔额子出在什么地方，也得预先商量好。
en: The key was to find a large Shanghai grain merchant who would first supply a quantity of unpolished rice for delivery to Ni Liangyao, then receive Zhejiang's grain when it arrived. In other words, the merchant would sell first and buy later. Naturally, the purchase and sale prices would differ, as would the quality of the rice. Grain-tax rice was of very poor quality, so compensation would be needed, together with an allowance for handling losses. The source of that money had to be agreed in advance.

zh: “事到如今，说不得，只好在今年新漕上打主意，加收若干。目前只有请藩库垫一垫。”
en: “At this stage, there is no alternative,” the grain intendant said. “We shall have to add something to the collection of this year's new grain. For the moment, the provincial treasury must advance the money.”

zh: “藩库先垫可以。”麟桂答复督粮道说，“不过你老哥也要替兄弟想一想，这个责任我实在担不起，总要抚台有公事，我才可以动支。
en: “The treasury can advance it,” Lingui replied, “but you must consider my position too. I truly cannot bear this responsibility. I need an official instruction from the governor before releasing funds.”

zh: “要公事恐怕办不到，要抚台一句切实的话，应该有的。现在大家同船合命，大人请放心，将来万一出了什么纰漏，我是证人。”
en: “A written instruction will probably be impossible. A definite verbal undertaking should be obtainable. We're all in the same boat now. Rest assured: if anything goes wrong later, I shall bear witness.”

zh: 话说到如此，麟桂只得点点头答应：“也只好这样了。”
en: With matters put so plainly, Lingui could only nod. “Then that will have to do.”

zh: “至于以后的事，”督粮道拱拱手对王有龄说：“一切都要偏劳！”
en: “As for what follows,” the grain intendant said to Wang with clasped hands, “we must leave the work to you.”

zh: 这句话王有龄却有些答应不下，因为他对上海的情形不熟，而且江宁一失，人心惶惶，粮商先垫出一批粮食，风险甚大，有没有人肯承揽此事，一点把握都没有。
en: Wang found that harder to accept. He knew little of Shanghai. With Jiangning lost and everyone anxious, supplying so much grain in advance would entail great risk. He had no idea whether a merchant would undertake it.

zh: 看他迟疑，督粮道便又说：“王兄，你不必怕！我刚才说过，这件事大家休戚相关，倘有为难之处，当然大家想办法，不会让你一个人坐蜡。王兄，你新铏初发，已见长才，佩服之至，尽管放手去干。
en: Seeing his hesitation, the intendant reassured him. “There is no need to be afraid. As I said, our interests are bound together. If difficulties arise, we shall all find a solution. We won't leave you alone in trouble. You have only just begun, Brother Wang, yet your ability is already evident. I admire it. Go ahead with confidence.”

zh: 受到这两句话的鼓励，工有龄想到了胡雪岩，该佩服的另有人。
en: Encouraged by these words, Wang thought of Hu. The man who deserved admiration was someone else.

zh: 谈到这里，事情可以算定局了，约定分头办事，麟桂和督粮道另行谒见抚台去谈差额的垫拨和将来如何开支？王有龄回去立刻便要设法去觅那肯垫出多少万石糙米的大粮商。
en: The matter was now settled, and they agreed to pursue their separate tasks. Lingui and the grain intendant would see Huang about advancing the price difference and accounting for it later. Wang would immediately find a merchant willing to supply the many tens of thousands of shi of rice required.

zh: 等一回海运局，第一个就问胡雪岩，说是从他回家以后，就没有来过，时己近午，想来他要在家吃了饭才来。但一直等到下午三点钟，还不见踪影，王有龄有些急了，他有许多事要跟胡雪岩商量，胡雪岩自己也应该知道，何以如此好整以暇？令人不解。
en: Upon returning to the bureau, his first question was for Hu. He was told that Hu had not come back since going home. It was nearly noon, so presumably he would come after lunch. Yet three o'clock arrived with no sign of him. Wang grew anxious. There was much to discuss, and Hu should know it. Why was he taking his time so calmly?

zh: 他没有想到，胡雪岩是叫张胖子缠住了。王有龄的出人意表的举动，使得信和上上下下，没有一个不是津津有味地资为话题。胡雪岩在店里的人缘原就不坏，当初被辞退时，实在因为他做事太荒唐，拆的烂污也太大，爱莫能助。以后又因为胡雪岩好面子，自觉落魄，不愿与敌人相见，所以渐渐疏远。现在重新唤起记忆，都说胡雪岩的眼光，确是厉害，手腕魄力也高人一等。如今且不说有海运局这一层关系，可以拉到一个大主顾，就没有这层关系，照胡雪岩的才干来说，信和如果想要发达，就应该把他请回来。
en: He had not imagined that Fat Zhang had detained him. Wang's unexpected visit had become the favourite topic of everyone at Xinhe. Hu had always been popular there. When he was dismissed, however, his conduct had seemed too outrageous and the trouble too great for anyone to help. Later, ashamed of his poverty, Hu avoided old acquaintances, and the ties had weakened. Now memories revived. Everyone said his judgement was exceptional, his methods and courage superior to other men's. Quite apart from the bureau connection and the important client it might bring, his abilities alone made him someone Xinhe ought to invite back if it wished to prosper.

zh: 这一下，张胖子的主意越坚定了。他原来就有些内疚于心，现在听大家的“口碑”，更有个人的利害关系在内，因为他们这些话传到东家耳朵里，一定会找了自己去问，别的都不说，一张五百两银子的借据，竟会弄丢了，这还成什么话？东家在绍兴还有一家钱庄，档手缺人，保不定会把自己调了过去，腾出空位子来请胡雪岩做，那时自己的颜面何存？
en: This strengthened Zhang's resolve. He had felt some guilt already. Hearing everyone's praise now added a personal concern. If their remarks reached the proprietor, Zhang would certainly be questioned. Even leaving everything else aside, how could he explain losing a note for five hundred taels? The proprietor had another bank in Shaoxing that needed a senior clerk. He might transfer Zhang there and make room for Hu. What would become of Zhang's dignity then?

zh: 为此他找了个知道胡雪岩住处的小徒弟带路，亲自出马。事先也盘算过一遍，胡雪岩四两银子一月的薪水，从离开信和之日起照补，十个月一共四十两银子，打了一张本票用红封袋封好，再备了茶叶、火腿两样礼物，登门拜访。
en: He therefore found a young apprentice who knew Hu's address and set out in person. His plan was ready. Hu's salary of four taels a month would be paid from the date of his departure: forty taels for ten months. Zhang had a bank note made out for that amount and put in a red envelope. With gifts of tea and ham, he went to call.

zh: 说也凑巧，等他从元宝街这头走过去，胡雪岩正好从海运局回家，自元宝街那头走过来，撞个正着，胡雪岩眼尖想避了开去，可是已经来不及了。
en: By chance, as he approached from one end of Yuanbao Street, Hu was returning from the bureau at the other. They met face to face. Hu saw him quickly and wanted to avoid him, but it was too late.

zh: “雪岩，雪岩！”张胖子跑得气喘吁吁地，面红心跳，这倒好，正可以掩饰他的窘色。
en: “Xueyan! Xueyan!” Zhang ran up, panting, his face red and heart pounding. That was useful: it concealed his embarrassment.

zh: “张先生！”胡雪岩恭恭敬敬的叫一声，“你老人家一向好？”
en: “Mr Zhang!” Hu greeted him respectfully. “Have you been well?”

zh: “好什么？”张胖子埋怨似他说，“从你一走，我好比砍掉一只右手，事事不顺。”
en: “Well?” Zhang sounded almost reproachful. “Since you left, I've been like a man who has lost his right hand. Nothing goes smoothly.”

zh: 胡雪岩心里有数，张胖子替人戴高帽子的本事极大，三言两语，就可以叫人晕晕糊糊，听他摆布，所以笑笑不答。
en: Hu knew his powers of flattery. A few words from Zhang could make a man so pleased with himself that he became easy to manipulate. Hu therefore smiled without answering.

zh: “雪岩！”张胖子从上到下把他打量了一遍，“你混得不错啊！”
en: “Xueyan!” Zhang examined him from head to foot. “You're doing rather well.”

zh: “托福！托福！”
en: “Thanks to your good wishes.”

zh: 胡雪岩只不说请他到家里坐的话，张胖子便骂小徒弟：“笨虫！把茶叶、火腿拎进去啊！”等小徒弟往胡家一走，张胖子也挪动了脚步，一面说道：“第一趟上门来看老伯母，总要意思意思，新茶陈火腿，是我自己的孝敬！”
en: Hu did not invite him inside. Zhang therefore scolded the apprentice. “You fool! Take the tea and ham into the house.” As the boy moved towards the gate, Zhang followed. “It's my first visit to your mother. I must bring a little something. Fresh tea and aged ham—a small token of my own respect.”

zh: 见些光景，胡雪岩只好请他到家里去坐。张胖子一定要拜见“老伯母”、“嫂夫人“。平民百姓的内外之防，没有官府人家那么严，胡雪岩的母亲和妻子都出来见了礼，听张胖子说了许多好听的话。
en: Hu had no choice but to invite him in. Zhang insisted on paying his respects to both Hu's mother and wife. Ordinary families observed less strict separation between men and women than official households, so both women came out, exchanged greetings, and heard many pleasant words from him.

zh: 等坐定了谈入正题。他把王有龄突然来到信和，还清那笔款子的经过，细说了一遍，只把遗失了那张借据这一节，瞒着不提。
en: Once they were seated, Zhang came to the point. He described Wang's unexpected visit and repayment in detail, omitting only the loss of the original note.

zh: 讲了事实，再谈感想，“雪岩！”他问，“你猜猜着，王老爷这一来，我顶顶高兴的是啥子？“
en: Then he turned from events to his feelings. “Xueyan, can you guess what pleased me most about His Honour's visit?”

zh: “自然是趁此可以拉住一个大主顾。”
en: “The chance to secure an important customer, naturally.”

zh: 这句话说到了张胖子的心里，但是他不肯承认：“不是。雪岩，并非我此刻卖好，要你见情，说实在的，当初那件事，东家大发脾气，我身为大伙，实在叫没法子，只好照店规行事。心里是这样在巴望，最好王老爷早早来还了这笔款子，或者让我发笔什么财，替你赔了那五百两头。这为什么？为来为去为的是你好重回信和。现在闲话少说喏，”他把预先备好的红封套取了出来，“他十十月的薪水，照补，四十两本票，收好了。走！”
en: That was precisely right, but Zhang would not admit it. “No. I'm not saying this to flatter you or make you grateful. The truth is that our employer was furious about that affair. As manager, I had no choice but to enforce the rules. All the while, I hoped Mr Wang would soon repay the money—or that I might come into a little fortune and cover the five hundred taels for you myself. Why? Simply so that you could return to Xinhe. Well, no more talk.” He produced the red envelope. “Here are ten months' back wages: a note for forty taels. Keep it safe. Come along!”

zh: 一面说，一面他用左手把红封套塞到胡雪岩手里，右手便来拉着他出门。
en: As he spoke, he pressed the envelope into Hu's hand with his left and seized him with his right to lead him out.

zh: “慢来，慢来！张先生。”胡雪岩问道：“怎的一桩事体，我还糊里糊涂。你说走，走到哪里去？”
en: “Wait a moment, Mr Zhang. I still don't understand what's happening. Where are we going?”

zh: “还有哪里？信和。”
en: “Where else? Xinhe.”

zh: 胡雪岩是明知故问，听他说明白了，便使劲摇头：“张先生，‘好马不吃回头草’，盛情心领，谢谢了。”说着把红封套退了回去。
en: Hu had asked deliberately. Once Zhang stated it plainly, he shook his head firmly. “A good horse doesn't turn back to graze the same patch. I appreciate your kindness, but no, thank you.” He handed the envelope back.

zh: 张胖子双手推拒，责备似他说：“雪岩，这就是你的不是了……
en: Zhang pushed it away with both hands. “Now, Xueyan, that isn't right of you...”

zh: 自此展开冗长的说服工作，他的口才虽好，胡雪岩的心肠也硬，随便他如何导之以理，动之以情，一个只是不肯松口。
en: A long campaign of persuasion followed. Zhang's eloquence met Hu's resolve. However he appealed to reason or feeling, Hu would not yield.

zh: 磨到日已过午，主人家留客便饭，实在也有逐客的意思。哪知张胖子是抱定了破釜沉舟的决心，嬲往胡雪岩，再也不肯走的，“好，多时不见，正要叙叙，我来添茶！”他摸出块碎银子，大声唤那小徒弟：“小瘌痢，到巷口‘皇饭儿’，叫他们送四样菜来：木榔豆腐，件儿肉，响铃儿，荤素菜，另外打两斤‘竹叶青’！”
en: By midday, the household invited him to stay for lunch, partly hoping that the offer would prompt him to leave. But Zhang had resolved to stake everything on success and would not let go. “Excellent! It's been so long since we talked properly. I'll add something to the meal.” He took out a piece of silver and shouted to the apprentice, “You little scamp! Go to the eating house at the end of the lane. Have them send four dishes: mulang tofu, sliced pork, crisp bean-curd rolls, and mixed meat and vegetables. And fetch two jin of Zhuyeqing wine.”

zh: 胡雪岩夫妇要拦拦不住，只好由他。等一喝上酒，胡雪岩就不便“闷声大发财”，听他一个人去说，少不得要找出许许多多理由来推托。无奈张胖子那张嘴十分厉害，就象《封神榜》斗法似地，胡雪岩每祭一样法宝，他总有办法来破，倒是有样法宝，足可使他无法招架，但胡雪岩不肯说，如果肯说破跟王有龄的关系，现在要到海运局去“做官”了，难道张胖子还能一定叫他回信和去立柜台，当伙计？
en: Hu and his wife could not stop him. Once the wine was served, Hu could no longer remain silently on the defensive while Zhang did all the talking. He had to invent one reason after another for refusing. But Zhang's tongue was formidable. Like the magical duels in The Investiture of the Gods, every weapon Hu produced was met by a counterspell. There was one argument Zhang could not answer, but Hu was unwilling to use it. If he revealed his relationship with Wang and his forthcoming work at the bureau, could Zhang possibly insist that he return to stand behind a bank counter?

zh: 酒添了又添，话越说越多，连胡雪岩的妻子都有些不耐烦了，正在这不得开交的当儿，来了个不速之客。
en: More wine was brought, and the conversation grew longer. Even Hu's wife began to lose patience. Just as the situation seemed impossible to resolve, an unexpected visitor arrived.

zh: “咦！”张胖子把眼睛瞪得好大，“高二爷，你怎么寻到这里来了？”
en: “Oh!” Zhang stared. “Second Master Gao! How did you find your way here?”

zh: 奉命来请胡雪岩的高升，机变虽快，却也一时无从回答，但他听出张胖子的语气有异，不知其中有何蹊跷？不敢贸然道破来意，愣在那里只拿双眼看着胡雪岩。
en: Sent to fetch Hu, Gao was quick-witted but could not answer immediately. Something in Zhang's tone seemed strange. Unsure what lay behind it, he dared not announce his purpose and merely looked at Hu.

zh: 看看是瞒不住了，其实也不必瞒，于是胡雪岩决定把他最后一样法宝拿出来。不过说来话长，先得把高升这里料理清楚。才能从容细叙。
en: The truth could no longer be concealed—and perhaps need not be. Hu decided to use his final argument. But it would take time to explain. First he must settle Gao's business, then tell the story at leisure.

zh: “你吃了饭没有？”胡雪岩先很亲切地问，“现成的酒菜，坐下来‘摆’一杯！”
en: “Have you eaten?” he asked warmly. “There's food and wine ready. Sit down and have a cup.”

zh: “不敢当，谢谢您老！”高升答道：“胡少爷不知什么时候得空？”
en: “Thank you, but I wouldn't presume. When will you be free, Young Master Hu?”

zh: “我知道了。”他看一看桌上的自鸣钟说：“我准四点钟到。”
en: “I understand.” Hu glanced at the clock on the table. “I'll be there at four precisely.”

zh: “那么，请胡少爷到公馆个吃便饭好了。”
en: “Then please come to the residence for dinner.”

zh: 把来意交代清楚，高升走了。胡雪岩才歉意地笑道：“实不相瞒，张先生，我已经跟王老爷先见过面了。我不陪他到信和去，其中自有道理，此刻也不必多说。王老爷约我到海运局帮忙，我已经答应了他，故而不好再回‘娘家‘。张先生你要体谅我的苦衷。“
en: With his message delivered, Gao left. Hu smiled apologetically. “To tell you the truth, Mr Zhang, I had already seen Mr Wang before he visited Xinhe. I had reasons for not accompanying him, though there's no need to discuss them now. He has invited me to help at the Sea Transport Bureau, and I've agreed. So I cannot return to my old home. You must understand my difficulty.”

zh: “啊！”张胖子咧丑嘴拉长了声调，做出那意想不到而又惊喜莫名的神态，“雪岩，恭喜，恭喜！你真正是‘鲤鱼跳龙门’了。
en: “Ah!” Zhang drew out the sound, opening his mouth in a display of astonished delight. “Congratulations, Xueyan! You truly are a carp that has leapt the Dragon Gate.”

zh: “跳了龙门，还是鲤鱼，为人不可忘本。我是学的钱庄生意，同行都是我一家。张先生，以后还要请你多照应。”
en: “Even after leaping the gate, I remain a carp. A man mustn't forget his beginnings. Banking is the trade I learned, and everyone in it is family to me. I shall still rely on your help.”

zh: “哪里话，哪里话！现在自然要请你照应。”张胖子忽然放低了声音说，“眼前就要靠你帮忙，我跟王老爷提过，想跟海运局做往来。现在银根松，摆在那里也可惜，你想个什么办法用它出去！回扣特别克己。”
en: “Not at all. It's we who must rely on you now.” Zhang suddenly lowered his voice. “In fact, there's something you can do at once. I told Mr Wang we'd like to do business with the bureau. Money is plentiful at present, and it's a pity to leave it idle. See if you can find a way to put ours to use. We'll be particularly generous about the commission.”

zh: “好！”胡雪岩很慎重地点头，“我有数了。”
en: “Very well.” Hu nodded seriously. “I'll bear it in mind.”

zh: 张胖子总算不虚此行，欣然告辞。胡雪岩也随即赶到王有龄公馆里。他把张胖子的神态语言形容了一番，两人拊掌大笑，都觉得是件很痛快的事。
en: Zhang left pleased that the visit had not been wasted. Hu then hurried to Wang's residence. His account of Zhang's expressions and speeches made both men clap their hands and laugh. They found the affair thoroughly satisfying.

zh: “闲话少说，我有件正事跟你商量。”
en: “Enough of that. There's important business to discuss.”

zh: 王有龄把上院谒见抚台，以及与藩司、粮道会议的结果都告诉了胡雪岩，问他该如何办法？
en: Wang related his audience with the governor and the consultation with the treasurer and grain intendant, then asked what should be done.

zh: “事情是有点麻烦。不过商人图利，只要划得来，刀头上的血也要去舐，风险总有人肯背的，要紧的是一定要有担保。”
en: “It is a little complicated. But merchants seek profit. If the return is sufficient, they'll lick blood from a blade. Someone will accept the risk. What matters is having a guarantee.”

zh: “怎么样担保呢？”
en: “What sort of guarantee?”

zh: “最好，当然是我们浙江有公事给他们，这一层怕办不到，那就只有另想别法，法子总有的，我先要请问，要垫的漕米有多少？”
en: “An official undertaking from Zhejiang would be best, naturally. I doubt we can obtain that, so we must find another way. There will be one. First, how much grain must be advanced?”

zh: “我查过帐了，一共还缺十四万五千石。”
en: “I checked the accounts. The shortage is 145,000 shi.”

zh: “这数目也还不大。”胡雪岩说，“我来托钱庄保付，粮商总可以放心了。”
en: “That isn't such a large amount,” Hu said. “I'll arrange for a bank to guarantee payment. That should put the grain merchant at ease.”

zh: “好极了。是托信和？”
en: “Excellent. Through Xinhe?”

zh: “请信和转托上海的钱庄，这一节一定可以办得到。不过抚台那里总要有句话，我劝你直接去看黄抚台，省得其中传话有周折。”
en: “Xinhe can arrange it with a Shanghai bank. That can certainly be done. But we must have a definite word from the governor. I advise you to see him directly, rather than let the message pass through others.”

zh: “这个，”王有龄有些不以为然，“既然藩台、粮道去请示，当然有确实回话给我。似乎不必多此一举。”
en: “Well...” Wang was not convinced. “Since the treasurer and grain intendant are asking for instructions, they'll surely give me a definite answer. Another visit seems unnecessary.”

zh: “其中另有道理。”胡雪岩放低了声音说，“作兴抚合另有交代，譬如说，什么开销要打在里头，他不便自己开口，更不便跟藩台说，全靠你识趣，提他一个头，他才会有话交下来！”
en: “There's another reason.” Hu lowered his voice. “The governor may have further instructions—some expense he wants included, for example. He can't conveniently raise it himself, still less discuss it with the treasurer. He needs you to understand and provide an opening. Then he can tell you what he wants.”

zh: “啊！”王有龄恍然大悟，不断点头。
en: “Ah!” Wang understood and nodded repeatedly.

zh: “还有一层，藩台跟粮道那里也要去安排好。就算他们自己清廉，手底下的人，个个眼红，谁不当你这一趟是可以‘吃饱’的好差使？没有好处，一定要出花样。”
en: “There's more. You must make arrangements at the treasury and the grain intendant's office too. Even if the men themselves are honest, their subordinates will all be envious. Who won't suppose this assignment offers you a chance to fill your pockets? Without some benefit, they're certain to make difficulties.”

zh: 王有龄越发惊奇了，“真正想不到！雪岩，”他说，“你做官这么内行！”
en: Wang was more astonished than ever. “I would never have thought of it. Xueyan, you're an expert at official life!”

zh: “做官跟做生意的道理是一样的。”
en: “The principles of being an official and doing business are the same.”

zh: 听得这话，王有龄有些想笑。但仔细想一想，胡雪岩的话虽话得直率，却是鞭辟入里的实情。反正这件事一开头就走的是小路，既然走了小路，就索性把它走通。只要浙江的漕粮交足，不误朝廷正用，其他都好商量。如果小路走得半途而废，中间出了乱子，虽有上司在上面顶着，但出面的是自己，首当其冲，必受大害。
en: Wang almost laughed. On reflection, however, blunt as the remark was, it went straight to the truth. This affair had begun by taking a side path. Having chosen it, they might as well follow it through. So long as Zhejiang's full grain quota was delivered and the state's needs were not delayed, everything else could be arranged. If they faltered halfway and trouble arose, their superiors might stand above them, but Wang was the man acting openly. He would bear the first and heaviest blow.

zh: 这样一想，他就觉得胡雪岩的话，真个是“金玉良言”。这个人也是自己万万少不得的。
en: Seen in that light, Hu's advice was truly worth its weight in gold. He was a man Wang could not do without.

zh: “雪岩，我想这样，我马上替你报捐，有了‘实收’，谁也不能说你不是一个官。那一来，你在我局里的名义就好看了，起码是个委员，办事也方便些。“
en: “Xueyan, here's what I propose. I'll apply to purchase a title for you at once. Once you have the official receipt, no one can deny you're an official. Your position in the bureau will then be more presentable—at least that of a commissioner—and you'll find it easier to act.”

zh: “这慢慢来！等你这一趟差使弄好了再说。”
en: “There's no hurry. Let's finish this assignment of yours first.”

zh: 王有龄懂他的意思。自己盘算着这一趟差使，总可以弄个三五千两银子，那时候替胡雪岩捐个官，可以捐大些。胡雪岩大概是这样在希望，自然要依他。
en: Wang understood what he thought Hu meant. The assignment should yield three to five thousand taels, he reckoned. Then he could purchase a more substantial title for his friend. Presumably that was what Hu hoped for, and naturally he should oblige him.

zh: “也许。”他把话说明了，“我有了钱，首先就替你办这件事。不过，眼前怎么样呢？总要有个名义，你才好替我出面。”
en: “Very well,” he said plainly. “Once I have the money, that will be the first thing I do for you. But what about now? You need some recognised position if you're to act for me.”

zh: “不必。”胡雪岩说，“我跟你的交情，有张胖子到外面去一说，大家都知道了，替你出面办什么事，人家自然相信。”
en: “There's no need,” Hu replied. “Once Zhang has told people about our friendship, everyone will know. Whatever I undertake on your behalf, they'll naturally trust me.”

zh: “好，好，都随你！”就从这一刻起，王有龄对他便到了言听计从的地步。
en: “Very well. As you wish.” From that moment, Wang came to follow Hu's advice in everything.

zh: 当天夜里又把酒细谈，各抒抱负。王有龄幼聆庭训，深知州县官虽被视作“风尘俗吏”，其实颇可有所展布，而且读书不成，去而捐官，既然走上了这条路子，也就断了金马玉堂的想头，索性作个功名之士。胡雪岩的想法比他还要实际，一个还脱不了“做官”的念头，一个则以为“行行出状元”，而以发财为第一，发了财照样亦可以做官，不过捐班至多捐一个三品的道员，没有红顶子戴而已。
en: That night, over more wine, they spoke at length of their ambitions. From his father's teaching, Wang knew that local magistrates, dismissed by some as ordinary officials immersed in worldly affairs, could in fact accomplish much. Since his studies had not brought success and he had purchased office, he had already abandoned dreams of the scholarly splendour of court. He would seek achievement and advancement along the practical path he had chosen. Hu's ideas were more practical still. One man remained attached to the ambition of official service; the other believed that excellence could be found in every trade and put making a fortune first. Wealth could bring office too. The only limitation was that purchased advancement reached no higher than a third-rank circuit intendancy, without the red hat button of a higher official.

zh: 因为气质相类，思路相近，所以越谈越投机，都觉得友朋之乐，胜过一切。当夜谈到三更过后，才由高升提着海运局的灯笼，送他回家。
en: Their temperaments and outlooks were so alike that the longer they talked, the better they understood each other. Both felt that the pleasure of friendship surpassed everything else. It was after midnight when Gao finally escorted Hu home, carrying a lantern bearing the bureau's name.

zh: 胡雪岩精力过人，睡得虽迟，第二天依旧一早起身。这天要办的一件大事，就是到信和去看张胖子。他心里在想，空手上门，面子上不好看，总得有所点缀才好。
en: Hu had exceptional energy. Despite the late night, he rose early the next morning. His main task was to visit Zhang at Xinhe. He felt that arriving empty-handed would look poor; some appropriate gesture was needed.

zh: 胡雪岩又想，送礼也不能送张胖子一个人。他为人素来“四海”，而现在正要展布手面，所以决定要博得个信和上下，皆大欢喜。
en: Nor should Zhang alone receive a present. Hu had always been generous in his dealings, and now that he had a chance to show it, he intended to please everyone at the bank.

zh: 这又不是仅仅有钱便可了事。他很细心地考虑到他那些老同事的关系、境遇、爱好，替每人备一份礼，无不投其所好，这费了他一上午的工夫，然后雇一个挑伕，挑着这一担礼物，跟着他直到盐桥信和钱庄。
en: Money alone would not do. He carefully considered each former colleague's circumstances, relationships, and tastes, then chose a gift suited to each. This occupied the whole morning. Finally, he hired a porter to carry the load and followed him to Xinhe at Salt Bridge.

zh: 这一下，就把信和上上下下都收服了。大家都有这佯一个感觉，胡雪岩倒霉时，不会找朋友的麻烦，他得意了，一定会照应朋友。
en: That won the entire bank over. Everyone felt the same thing: when Hu was unfortunate, he did not trouble his friends; when he prospered, he would always remember them.

zh: 当然，最兴奋的是张胖子，昨天他从胡家出来，不回钱庄，先去拜访东家，自诩“慧眼识英雄”，早已看出胡雪岩不是池中物，因而平时相待极厚。
en: Zhang was naturally the most excited. After leaving Hu's house the previous day, he had gone to the proprietor before returning to the bank. He boasted of his ability to recognise exceptional men. He had long known that Hu was destined for greater things, he said, and had always treated him especially well.

zh: 胡雪岩所以当初去而无怨，以及现在仍旧不忘信和，都是为了他的情分。东家听了他这番“丑表功”，信以为真，着实嘉奖了他几句，而且也作了指示，海运局这个大主顾，一定要拉往，因为赚钱不赚钱在其次，声誉信用有关，这就是钱庄票号的资本，信和能够代理海运局的汇划，在上海的同行中，就要刮目相看了。
en: It was because of their bond that Hu had left without resentment and still remembered Xinhe with affection. The proprietor believed this shameless self-praise, commended Zhang warmly, and gave clear instructions: the bureau must be secured as a client. Profit was secondary. Reputation and credit were involved, and those were a bank's real capital. If Xinhe handled the bureau's remittances, its Shanghai counterparts would regard it with new respect.

zh: 张胖子和胡雪岩都是很厉害的角色，关起门来谈生意，都不肯泄漏真意，胡雪岩说：“今天我遇见王老爷，谈起跟信和往来的事。他告诉我，现在有两三家钱庄，都要放款给海运局，也不是放款，是垫拨，因为利息有上落，还没有谈定局，听说是我的来头，情形当然不同。张先生，你倒开个‘盘口’看！”
en: Both Zhang and Hu were formidable men. Behind closed doors, neither would reveal his true intentions. Hu began, “When I saw Mr Wang today, we discussed doing business with Xinhe. He said two or three banks were offering loans to the bureau—or rather, advances. Nothing has been settled because the interest rates differ. Naturally, when he heard that I was speaking for you, the situation changed. Mr Zhang, what terms would you offer?”

zh: 张胖子先不答这句话，只问：“是哪两三家？”
en: Zhang did not answer directly. “Which banks?”

zh: 胡雪岩笑了：“这，人家怎么肯说？”
en: Hu smiled. “How would anyone be willing to tell me that?”

zh: “那么，你说，利息明的多少，暗的多少？”
en: “Then tell me this: what is the rate on paper, and what is the private arrangement?”

zh: “现在不谈暗的，只谈明的好了。”
en: “Let's leave private arrangements aside for now and discuss the stated rate.”

zh: “话是这么说，”张胖子放低了声音，“你自己呢？加多少帽子？”
en: “Certainly,” Zhang said, lowering his voice. “But what about you? How much do you want added for yourself?”

zh: 胡雪岩大摇其头：“王老爷托我的事，我怎么好落他的‘后手’？这也不必谈。”
en: Hu shook his head vigorously. “Mr Wang has entrusted this to me. How could I take a secret cut behind his back? There's nothing to discuss on that score.”

zh: “你不要，我们总要意思意思。”张胖子又问，“要垫多少？期限是长是短，你先说了好筹划。”
en: “Even if you ask for nothing, we must show our appreciation.” Zhang continued, “How much is needed, and for how long? Tell me that first so I can make arrangements.”

zh: “总要二十万。”
en: “At least two hundred thousand taels.”

zh: “二十万？”张胖子吃惊地说，“信和的底子你知道的，这要到外面去调。”
en: “Two hundred thousand?” Zhang was startled. “You know Xinhe's resources. We'd have to raise money elsewhere.”

zh: 到同行中去调头寸，利息就要高了，胡雪岩懂得他的用意，便笑笑说道：“那就不必谈下去了。”
en: Obtaining funds from other banks would mean a higher interest rate. Hu understood the implication and smiled. “Then there's no point in discussing it further.”

zh: “不是这话，不是这话！”张胖子又急忙改口，“你的来头，信和一定要替你做面子，再多些也要想办法。这你不管了，你说，期限长短？”
en: “That's not what I mean!” Zhang hastily corrected himself. “Since you bring us the business, we must do you credit. Even a larger sum could be managed. Leave that to us. Tell me the term.”

zh: “你们喜欢长，还是喜欢短？”胡雪岩说，“长是长的办法，短是短的办法。”如果期限能够放长，胡雪岩预备移花接木，借信和的本钱，开自己的钱庄。
en: “Would you prefer a long one or a short one? We can arrange either accordingly.” If the term could be extended, Hu intended to use a substitution of his own and open a bank with Xinhe's capital.

zh: 张胖子自然不肯明白表示，只说：“主随客便，要你这里吩咐下来，我们才好去调度。”
en: Zhang naturally avoided stating a preference. “We follow the client's wishes. Once you tell us what is required, we can arrange our funds.”

zh: 这一问胡雪岩无从回答，海运局现在还不需用现银，只要信和能够担保。而他自己呢，虽然灵机一动，想借信和的资本来开钱庄，但这件事到底要跟王有龄从长计议过了，才有动手，眼前也还说不出个所以然来。
en: Hu could not answer that. The bureau did not yet need cash; it needed Xinhe's guarantee. As for his own sudden idea of using Xinhe's capital to establish a bank, he would have to discuss it thoroughly with Wang before acting. He had no definite plan to state.

zh: 他这样踌躇着，张胖子却误会了，以为胡雪岩还是想在利息上“戴帽子”，自己不便开口，所以他作了个暗示：“雪岩，我们先谈一句自己弟兄的私话，你现在做了官，排场总要的，有些用度，自己要垫，我开个折子给你，二千两的额子以内，随时支用，你有钱随时来归，利息不计。”
en: Zhang misunderstood his hesitation, assuming that Hu did want a personal margin added to the interest but was embarrassed to say so. He offered a hint. “Xueyan, let us speak privately as friends. Now that you've entered official life, you must keep up appearances, and some expenses will have to be advanced from your own pocket. I'll open an account for you. Draw whatever you need up to two thousand taels and repay it whenever you have the money. No interest.”

zh: 胡雪岩明白，这是信和先送二千两银子，得人钱财，与人消灾，收了他这二千两，信和有什么要求，就非得替他办到不可。不过胡雪岩也不便峻拒，故意吹句牛：“这倒不必。信和是我‘娘家’，我有钱不存信和存哪里？过几天我有笔款子，大概五六千两，放在你们这里，先做个往来。”
en: Hu understood: Xinhe was offering two thousand taels in advance. Accept a man's money, and you must solve his problems. If he took it, he would have to fulfil the bank's requests. But an outright refusal would be awkward. Instead, he deliberately boasted. “There's no need. Xinhe is my old home. Where else would I deposit my money? In a few days, I expect five or six thousand taels. I'll leave it here and begin an account.”

zh: “那太好了。你拿来我替你放，包你利息好。”
en: “Excellent! Bring it in, and I'll lend it out for you. I guarantee a good return.”

zh: “这再谈吧！”胡雪岩问道：“信和现在跟上海‘三大’往来多不多？”
en: “We can discuss that later. Do you have much business with Shanghai's Big Three at present?”

zh: “还好。”
en: “Fairly well.”

zh: 这就是不多之意，胡雪岩心里有些嘀咕，考虑了一会，觉得不能再兜圈子了，尔虞我诈，大家不说实后，弄到头来，会出乱子。
en: That meant not much. Hu was uneasy. After considering it, he decided they could no longer circle around each other. If both continued bluffing and concealing the truth, the matter would end in trouble.

zh: 于是他换了副神态说：“我也知道你的意思，海运局跟你做了往来，信和这块牌子就格外响了。我总竭力拉拢。不过眼前海运局要信和帮忙。这个忙帮成功，好处不在少数。”
en: His manner changed. “I understand what you want. A relationship with the bureau would make Xinhe's name more distinguished, and I'll do my best to bring it about. But first the bureau needs your help. If you can provide it, the benefits will be substantial.”

zh: 一听这话，张胖子越发兴奋，连连答应：“一定效劳，一定效劳。”
en: Zhang grew still more eager. “Certainly. We shall do everything we can.”

zh: “话未说之先，我有句话要交代。”胡雪岩神色凛然地，“今天我跟你谈的事，是抚台交下来的，泄漏不得半点！倘或泄漏出去，闯出祸来，不要说我，王老爷也救不了你，做官的人不讲道理，那时抚台派兵来封信和的门，你不要怪我。”
en: “Before I explain, there is one condition.” Hu's expression became stern. “What we discuss today comes from the governor. Not a word may leak out. If it does and trouble follows, neither I nor Mr Wang will be able to save you. Officials aren't reasonable when things go wrong. If the governor sends soldiers to seal Xinhe's doors, don't blame me.”

zh: 说得如此严重，把笑口常开的张胖子吓得脸色发青，“唷！”他说，“这不是当玩儿的。等我把门来关起来。“
en: The warning wiped the smile from Zhang's face and left him pale. “Oh! This is no joking matter. Let me close the door.”

zh: 关上房门，两个并坐在僻处，胡雪岩把那移花接木之计，约略说了一遍，问张胖子两点：第一，有没有熟识的粮商可以介绍。第二，肯不肯承诺保付。
en: With the door shut, they sat together in a secluded corner. Hu outlined the substitution scheme and asked two questions: did Zhang know a grain merchant he could recommend, and would Xinhe guarantee payment?

zh: 这风险太大了。张胖子一时答应不下，站起来绕室徘徊，心里不住盘算。
en: The risk seemed enormous. Zhang could not agree at once. He rose and walked about the room, calculating silently.

zh: 胡雪岩见此光景，觉得有动之以利的必要，便把他拉住坐下，低声又说：“风险你自己去看，除非杭州到上海这一段水路上，出了纰漏，漕船沉掉，漕米无法归垫，不然不会有风险的。至于你们的好处，这样，好在日子不多，从承诺保付之日起，海运局就算借了信和的现银子，照日拆计息，一直到跟粮商交割清楚为止。你看如何？”
en: Seeing this, Hu decided to appeal to his interest. He drew him back into a seat and spoke quietly. “Judge the risk for yourself. Unless something happens on the waterway between Hangzhou and Shanghai—unless the grain boats sink and the rice cannot be supplied in repayment—there should be no loss. As for your return, here's my proposal. The period won't be long. From the day you undertake the guarantee, the bureau will treat the sum as though it had borrowed cash from Xinhe, paying interest by the day until the merchant's account is fully settled. How does that sound?”

zh: 这一说，张胖子怦怦心动了，不须调动头寸，只凭一纸契约，就可以当作放出现款，收取利息，这是不用本钱的生意，加以还可借海运局来长自己的声势，岂不大妙？
en: Zhang's heart stirred. Without moving any funds, a written undertaking would earn interest as though he had made a cash loan. It was business requiring no immediate capital, with the bureau's reputation to enhance his own. What could be better?

zh: 张胖子利害相权，心思已经活动、做生意原来就是靠眼光，有胆气，想到胡雪岩当初放那五百两银子给王有龄，还不是眼光独到，甚至连张“饭票子”都赔在里面，在他个人来说，是背了风险，但如今来看，这笔生意他是做对了。
en: Weighing advantage against danger, he began to yield. Business depended on judgement and courage. Hadn't Hu shown unusual judgement in lending those five hundred taels to Wang? He had even sacrificed his livelihood over it. Personally, he had borne a great risk. Yet now the transaction had proved sound.

zh: 由于胡雪岩的现成的例子摆着，张胖子的胆便大了，心思也灵活了，他已决定接受胡雪岩的建议，但不便当时就作决定，还有一件事是非做不可的，到藩台衙门去摸一摸底，看看漕米运到上海的情形，藩台对王有龄是怎样一种态度？只有这两层上没有什么疑问，这笔生意就算做定了。
en: With Hu's example before him, Zhang grew bolder and more inventive. He had decided to accept, but could not commit immediately. There was one thing he must do first: inquire at the provincial treasury about the grain's progress towards Shanghai and the treasurer's attitude to Wang. If both points were satisfactory, the business was settled.

zh: 于是他说：“雪岩！我们自己弟兄，还有说不通、相信不过的地方？这就算八成帐了！不过象这样大的进出，我总要向东家说一声，准定明天午刻听回话，你看好不好？”
en: “Xueyan, between friends like us, what cannot be discussed or trusted?” he said. “Consider it eight-tenths agreed. But for a transaction this size, I must consult my employer. I'll give you a definite answer by noon tomorrow. Will that do?”

zh: “这有什么不好？不过我也有句话，大家都是替人家办事，身不由主。我老实说，也不必明天午刻，索性到后天好了，一过后灭，没有回话，我也就不必再来看你，省得白耽误工夫。“
en: “Of course. But I have something to say too. We're both acting for others and cannot decide everything ourselves. To be frank, there's no need to insist on noon tomorrow. Take until the day after. If I hear nothing by then, I won't come back. That will save us both wasted time.”

zh: 这就是说定了一个最后限期。张胖子觉得胡雪岩做事爽快而有担当，十分欣赏，连连点头答应。
en: A final deadline had been set. Zhang admired Hu's decisiveness and willingness to take responsibility, and nodded repeatedly.

zh: 回到海运局跟王有龄见面，互道各人商谈的结果。王有龄十分兴奋，说这天上午非常顺利，先去看了麟桂，说抚台已有表示，差额由藩库先垫，今年新漕中如何加派来弥补这笔款子，到时候再定办法，不与王有龄相干。又去看了抚台，黄宗汉吩咐，只要事情办得快，多花点钱无所谓。他还拿出两道上谕来给王有龄看，一道是八旗京兵有十五万之多，须严加训练，欠饷要设法发清，通谕各省，从速解运漕米银两，以供正用。一道是酌减文武大臣“养廉”银，以充军饷。可见得朝廷在粮饷上调度困难，如能早日运到，黄宗汉答应特保王有龄升官。
en: Back at the bureau, Hu and Wang exchanged reports. Wang was delighted: his morning had gone very well. He had first seen Lingui, who said the governor had agreed that the treasury should advance the price difference. How it would later be recovered through additional levies on the new grain would be decided separately and was no concern of Wang's. He had then seen Huang, who told him that some extra expense did not matter provided the work was done quickly. The governor showed him two edicts. One stated that the capital's Eight Banner forces numbered 150,000, required strict training, and must receive their overdue pay; the provinces were to expedite grain and silver to meet the state's needs. The other ordered reductions in civil and military officials' integrity allowances to supply military funds. Clearly, the court was struggling to meet its requirements. Huang promised to recommend Wang for promotion if the grain arrived promptly.

zh: “照这一说，事情就差不多了。”胡雪岩心知张胖子要去打听情形，既然藩司有此确实表示，信和这方面当然可以放心，不必等张胖子正式回话，便可知事已定局，“该商量商量，好动身到上海去寻‘户头’了。”
en: “Then the matter is almost settled.” Hu knew Zhang would make inquiries. With the treasury's undertaking so definite, Xinhe could feel secure. There was no need to await Zhang's formal reply to know the outcome. “We should discuss going to Shanghai to find the right merchant.”

zh: “我想这样，请你陪了我去，局里当然要派两个人，那不过摆摆样子，事情全靠你来办。”
en: “My thought is that you should accompany me. The bureau will naturally send two officials, but that will be largely for appearances. The real work will depend on you.”

zh: 胡雪岩想了想答道：“真的要我来办，得要听我的办法。”
en: Hu considered. “If you truly want me to handle it, you must let me do it my way.”

zh: “好！”王有龄毫不迟疑地答就，“全听你的。”
en: “Certainly,” Wang answered without hesitation. “I'll follow your lead.”

zh: 为了办事方便，王有龄到底下了一通“关书”，聘请胡雪岩当“司事”，在签押房旁边一个小房间办事，作幕后的策划。首先是从藩库提了十万两银子过来，等跟信和谈好了保付的办法，把这笔款子存入信和，先划三万两到上海大亨钱庄。这三万两银子，一万两作公费使用，二万两要替黄宗汉汇到家乡，当然那是极秘密的。
en: To make the work easier, Wang finally issued a formal letter engaging Hu as an administrative clerk. He occupied a small room beside the private office and planned matters behind the scenes. First, a hundred thousand taels were drawn from the provincial treasury. Once the guarantee terms with Xinhe had been settled, the sum was deposited there, and thirty thousand taels were remitted to Daheng Bank in Shanghai. Of that amount, ten thousand were for official expenses; twenty thousand were to be forwarded to Huang Zonghan's home district. The latter arrangement was, of course, strictly secret.

zh: 然后，胡雪岩在局里挑了两个委员，一个是麟桂的私人姓周，一个跟粮道有关系姓吴，请王有龄下条子，“派随赴沪”，同时每人额外先送二百两银子的旅费，周、吴二人原来有些敌视胡雪岩，等打听列这于排出于他的主张，立刻便倾心结交。
en: Hu then selected two bureau commissioners: Zhou, a follower of Lingui, and Wu, who had connections with the grain intendant. He asked Wang to issue orders assigning them to accompany him to Shanghai. Each also received an additional two hundred taels for travelling expenses. Both had initially regarded Hu with some hostility, but once they learned that this payment was his proposal, they immediately sought his friendship.

zh: 胡雪岩又把张胖子也邀在一起，加上庶务、厨子、听差、上上下下一共十个人，雇了两只“无锡快”，随带大批准备送人的土产，从杭州城内第一座大桥“万安桥”下船，解缆出关，沿运河东行。
en: Hu invited Zhang as well. With the general affairs officer, cook, attendants, and others, the party numbered ten. They hired two fast Wuxi boats and took a large supply of local products intended as gifts. Boarding at Wan'an Bridge, the first great bridge within Hangzhou, they cast off, passed the city barrier, and travelled east along the canal.

zh: 这时是三月天气，两岸平畴，绿油油的桑林，黄澄澄的菜花，深红浅绛的桃李，织成一幅锦绣平原。工有龄诗兴大发，倚舷闲眺，吟哦不绝。但别的人没有他那么雅兴，周、吴两委员，加上胡雪岩、张胖子正好凑成一桌麻将。
en: It was the third month. Flat fields, rich green mulberry groves, golden rapeseed flowers, and peach and plum blossoms in shades of red and pink spread along both banks like a brocade. Inspired to poetry, Wang leaned against the side of his boat, gazing and murmuring lines. The others had no such literary inclination. Zhou and Wu, together with Hu and Zhang, made exactly four for mahjong.

zh: 打牌是张胖子所提议的，胡雪岩欣然附议。张胖子便要派人到头一条船上去请周、吴二人，一个说，“慢慢！摆好桌子再说。”
en: Zhang proposed the game, and Hu readily agreed. Zhang was about to send to the leading boat for the two commissioners when Hu stopped him. “Wait. Let's have the table ready first.”

zh: 胡雪岩早有准备的，打开箱子，取出簇新的一副竹背牙牌，极精致的一副筹码，雪白的牙牌，叫船家的女儿阿珠来铺好桌子，分好筹码。两面茶几，摆上果碟，泡上好茶，然后叫船家停一停船，搭上跳板，把周、吴两委员请了过来。
en: Hu had come prepared. He opened a trunk and took out a new set of ivory mahjong tiles with bamboo backs and an exquisite set of counters. He called the boatman's daughter, A'zhu, to lay the table and divide the counters. Fruit dishes stood on side tables, and fine tea was brewed. Only then did he ask the boatman to pause alongside the other vessel, put out a gangplank, and invite Zhou and Wu over.

zh: 一看这场面，两人都是高兴得不得了，“有趣，有趣！”周委员笑着说道：“跟我们这位胡大哥在一起，实在有劲道。”
en: The two were delighted by the preparations. “Splendid!” Zhou laughed. “There's real pleasure in travelling with our friend Hu.”

zh: “闲话少说，”吴委员更性急，“快坐下来。怎么打法？”
en: “Enough talk,” Wu said impatiently. “Let's sit down. What rules are we playing?”

zh: 于是四个人坐下来扳了位，张胖子提议，一百两银子一底的“幺半”，二十和底，三百和满贯。自摸一副“辣子”，三十两一家，便有九十两进帐。
en: They took their seats and drew for positions. Zhang proposed a game with a hundred taels to a stake, using the yaoban scoring scale: a twenty-point base and a three-hundred-point limit. A self-drawn limit hand would bring thirty taels from each of the other players, ninety in all.

zh: “太大了！”周委员说，“自己人小玩玩，打个对折吧！”
en: “That's too high,” Zhou said. “We're friends playing for amusement. Let's halve it.”

zh: “对，对，打对折。”吴委员也说，“我只带了三十两银子，不够输的。”
en: “Yes, halve it,” Wu agreed. “I've brought only thirty taels. I can't afford to lose at that rate.”

zh: “不要紧，不要紧！有钱庄的人在这里，两位怕什么？”胡雪岩一面说，一面给张胖子递了个眼色。
en: “No need to worry. With a banker here, what have you to fear?” As he spoke, Hu gave Zhang a meaningful glance.

zh: 张胖子会意了，从身上摸出一叠银票来，取了两张一百两的放在周，吴二人面前，笑着说道，“我先垫本，赢了我提一成。”
en: Zhang understood. Taking out a stack of bank drafts, he laid a hundred-tael note before each commissioner. “I'll provide the capital,” he said with a smile. “If you win, I take ten per cent.”

zh: “输了呢？”吴委员问。
en: “And if we lose?” Wu asked.

zh: “输了？”胡雪岩说，“等赢了再还。”
en: “If you lose,” Hu said, “repay it when you win.”

zh: 这是有赢无输的牌，周、吴二人越发高兴。心里痛快，牌风也顺了，加以明慧可人的阿珠，一遍遍毛巾把子，一道道点心送了上来，这场牌打得实在舒服。
en: It was a game in which they could win without really losing. Zhou and Wu were happier still. Good spirits brought good luck, and the bright, charming A'zhu repeatedly supplied hot towels and refreshments. Nothing could have made the game more comfortable.

zh: 四圈打完，坐在胡雪岩下家的周委员，一家大赢，吴委员也还不错，输的是张胖子和胡雪岩，两个人的牌品都好，依旧笑嘻嘻地毫不在乎。
en: After four rounds, Zhou, sitting immediately after Hu, had won heavily. Wu had done fairly well too. The losers were Zhang and Hu, both cheerful and gracious, apparently unconcerned.

zh: 等扳了位，吴委员的牌风又上去了，因为这四圈恰好是他坐在胡雪岩的下家。再下一家是周委员，吴委员只顾自己做大牌，张子出得松，所以周委员也还好，氽出去有限。
en: After they changed places, Wu's luck improved. For these next four rounds, it was he who sat after Hu. Zhou followed Wu, whose concentration on making high-scoring hands led him to discard freely. Zhou therefore did reasonably well too and lost little of what he had won.

zh: 八圈打完，船已泊岸，天也快黑了，自然歇手。算一算筹码，吴委员赢了一底半，周委员赢了一底，张胖子没有什么输赢。但有他们两家一成的贴补，也变成了赢家，只有胡雪岩一个人大输，连头钱在内，成了“四吃一”。
en: By the end of eight rounds, the boats had moored and darkness was approaching, so they stopped. Counting the counters, Wu had won a stake and a half, Zhou one stake. Zhang had neither won nor lost much, but the ten per cent due from their winnings made him a winner too. Hu alone had lost heavily. Including the table fee, there were four claims upon a single loser's purse.

zh: “摆着，摆着！”周委员很大方地说，“明天再打再算！”
en: “Leave it for now,” Zhou said generously. “We can play again tomorrow and settle then.”

zh: “赌钱赌个现！”胡雪岩说了句杭州的谚语，“而况是第一次，来，来兑筹码，兑筹码！”
en: “Gambling debts are paid in cash,” Hu replied with a Hangzhou saying. “Besides, this is our first game together. Come, let's exchange the counters.”

zh: 胡雪岩开“枕头箱”取出银票，一一照付，零数用现银子补足，只看他也不怎么细算，三把两把一抓，分配停当，各人自已再数一数，丝毫不差。
en: He opened his small bedside chest and took out bank drafts, paying each man and making up the odd amounts in silver. He seemed scarcely to calculate, merely taking a few handfuls and dividing them. Yet when the recipients checked, every payment was exact.

zh: 吴委员大为倾服，翘起大拇指赞道：“雪岩兄，‘度支才也’！”
en: Wu was greatly impressed and raised a thumb. “Brother Xueyan, you have the talent of a master of finance!”

zh: 他肚子里有些墨水，这句引自《新唐书》，唐明皇欣赏杨国忠替他管赌帐管得清楚的褒语，胡雪岩却听不懂，但他懂得藏拙，料想是句好话，只报以感谢的一笑，不多说什么！
en: Wu had some literary learning. The phrase came from the New Book of Tang, in which Emperor Xuanzong praised Yang Guozhong for keeping his gambling accounts so clearly. Hu did not understand the allusion, but he knew how to conceal a gap in his knowledge. Assuming it was a compliment, he merely smiled his thanks.

zh: 最后算头钱，那是一副牌、一副牌打的，因为牌风甚大，打了十六七两银子，胡雪岩把筹码往自己面前一放，喊道：“阿珠！”
en: Last came the table fee, collected hand by hand. With such high stakes, it amounted to sixteen or seventeen taels. Hu placed the counters before him and called, “A'zhu!”

zh: 阿珠正帮着她娘在船梢上做菜，听得招呼，娇滴滴答应一声：“来了！”
en: She was helping her mother cook at the stern. At his call, she answered brightly, “Coming!”

zh: 接着便出现在船门口，她系一条青竹布围裙，一面擦着手，一面憨憨地笑着，一根乌油油的长辫子从肩上斜甩了过来，衬着她那张红白分明的鹅蛋脸，那番风韵，着实撩人。
en: She appeared in the cabin doorway, wiping her hands on a blue cotton apron and smiling with simple good humour. Her long, glossy black plait had swung forward over one shoulder, setting off her oval face with its clear complexion and rosy colour. She was strikingly attractive.

zh: 胡雪岩眼尖，眼角已瞟见周、吴二人盯着阿珠不放的神情，心里立刻又有了盘算，“来，阿珠，四两银子的头钱。”他说：“交给你娘！”
en: Hu's quick eyes noticed Zhou and Wu staring at her, and another calculation formed in his mind. “Come here, A'zhu. Four taels in table fees,” he said. “Give them to your mother.”

zh: “谢谢胡老爷！”阿珠福了福。
en: “Thank you, Mr Hu.” She made a curtsy.

zh: “你谢错人了！要谢周老爷、吴老爷。喏！”他拈起一张银票，招一招手，等阿珠走近桌子，他才低声又说：“头钱不止四两。周老爷、吴老爷格外有赏，补足二十两银子，是你的私房钱。”
en: “You're thanking the wrong man. Thank Mr Zhou and Mr Wu. Here!” He picked up a bank draft and beckoned. When she came close to the table, he spoke softly. “The fees came to more than four taels. Mr Zhou and Mr Wu are adding a special reward to make twenty in all. It's money for you to keep yourself.”

zh: 这一说，阿珠的双眼张得更大了，惊喜地不知所措，张胖子便笑道：“阿珠！周老爷、吴老爷替你办嫁妆。还不快道谢！”
en: Her eyes opened wider, and she was too delighted and surprised to know what to do. Zhang laughed. “A'zhu, Mr Zhou and Mr Wu are helping with your dowry. Aren't you going to thank them?”

zh: “张老爷最喜欢说笑话！”阿珠红云满面，旋即垂着眼替周、吴二人请安。
en: “Mr Zhang is always joking!” She blushed deeply, then lowered her eyes and paid her respects to Zhou and Wu.

zh: “这倒不能不意思意思了！”吴委员向周委员说。于是每人又赏了十两。
en: “Now we must add something ourselves,” Wu said to Zhou. Each gave her another ten taels.

zh: 在阿珠，自出娘胎，何曾有过这么多钱？只看她道谢又道谢，站起身来晃荡着长辫子，碎步走向船梢，然后便是又喘又笑在说话的声音，想来是把这桩得意的快事在告诉她娘。
en: Never in her life had A'zhu possessed so much money. She thanked them again and again, then rose and hurried towards the stern, her long plait swinging. A moment later they heard breathless, laughing speech. She was evidently telling her mother of her good fortune.

zh: 大家都听得十分有趣，相视微笑。就这时听得外面在搭跳板，接着是船家招呼：“王大老爷走好！”
en: They all found it entertaining and exchanged smiles. Just then, a gangplank was laid outside, followed by the boatman's call: “Mind your step, Your Honour Wang!”

zh: 王有龄过船来了，大家一剂起身迎接，只见他手里拿着一个信笺，兴冲冲地走了进来，笑着问周、吴二人：“胜败如何？”
en: Wang had crossed over from his boat. Everyone rose to greet him as he entered cheerfully with a sheet of writing paper in his hand. Smiling, he asked Zhou and Wu, “How did the battle go?”

zh: 属官听上司提起赌钱的事，未免不好意思，周委员红着脸答道：“托大人的福！”
en: They were embarrassed to have their superior refer to the gambling. Zhou blushed. “Fortune favoured us, thanks to Your Excellency.”

zh: “好，好！”王有龄指着张胖子说，“想来是张老哥输了，饯庄大老板输几个不在乎。”
en: “Good, good.” Wang pointed to Zhang. “Then our banker must have lost. A few taels mean little to a man of his resources.”

zh: “理当报效，理当报效。”
en: “A pleasure to contribute, a pleasure.”

zh: 说笑了一会，阿珠来摆桌子开饭。“无锡快”上的“船菜”是有名的，这天又特别巴结，自然更精致了。
en: After some joking, A'zhu laid the table for dinner. The cooking aboard the fast Wuxi boats was famous, and special efforts had been made that day, so the food was finer still.

zh: 除此以外，各人都还带得有“路菜”，桌子上摆不下，另外端两张茶几来摆。胡雪岩早关照庶务多带陈年“竹叶青”，此时开了一坛，烫得恰到好处，斟在杯子里，糟香四溢，连一向不善饮的周委员，都忍不住想来一杯。
en: Everyone had also brought provisions for the journey. There was not enough room on the main table, and two side tables had to be added. Hu had instructed the general affairs officer to bring plenty of aged Zhuyeqing wine. A jar was opened and warmed to precisely the right temperature. Its rich aroma filled the air as it was poured. Even Zhou, ordinarily a poor drinker, could not resist a cup.

zh: 这样的场合，再有活色生香的阿珠侍席，应该是淳于髡所说的“饮可八斗”的境界，无奈有王有龄在座，大家便都拘束了，他谈话的对象也只是一个吴委员，这天下午倚舷平眺，做了四首七绝，题名《春望》，十分得意，此时兴高采烈地跟吴委员谈论，什么“这个字不响”，“那个字该用去声”，大家听不大懂，也没有兴致去听，但礼貌上又非装得很喜欢听不可的样子，以致于变成喝闷酒，嘉肴醇醒，淡而无味，可餐的秀色，亦平白地糟蹋了，真是耳朵受罪，还连带了眼睛受屈！
en: With such a meal and the lively, attractive A'zhu serving them, it should have been an occasion on which, as the ancient wit Chunyu Kun said, a man could drink an astonishing amount. Unfortunately, Wang's presence made everyone restrained. He conversed only with Wu. That afternoon, gazing from his boat, he had composed four seven-character quatrains entitled “Spring Views” and was very proud of them. Now he enthusiastically discussed which word lacked resonance and which should carry a departing tone. The others understood little and cared less, yet courtesy required them to look fascinated. They drank in gloomy silence. Fine food and mellow wine lost their flavour; even the girl's charms were wasted. Their ears suffered, and their eyes were deprived as well.

zh: 胡雪岩看看不是路数，一番细心安排，都叫王有龄的酸气给冲掉了。好在有约在先，此行凡事得听他作主，所以他找了个空隙，丢过去一个眼色，意思请他早些回自己的船，好让大家自由些。
en: Hu saw that things were going wrong. His careful arrangements were being spoiled by Wang's pedantry. Fortunately, they had agreed that Hu should direct this journey. Seizing a pause, he gave Wang a glance, asking him to return early to his own boat and leave the others free to enjoy themselves.

zh: 王有龄倒是酒酣耳热，谈得正痛快，所以对胡雪岩的暗示，起初还不能领会，看一看大家的神态，再细一想，方始明白，心头随即浮起歉意。
en: Warm with wine and delighted by his conversation, Wang at first missed the hint. Then he examined the others' expressions, thought a little, understood, and felt apologetic.

zh: “我的酒差不多了！”他也很机警，“你们慢慢喝。”
en: “I've had enough wine,” he said tactfully. “You carry on.”

zh: 于是叫阿珠盛了小半碗饭，王有龄吃完离席。胡雪岩知道他的酒不曾够，特地关照船家，另外备四个碟子，烫一斤酒送到前面船上。
en: He asked A'zhu for a small half-bowl of rice, ate it, and left the table. Hu knew that he had not really finished drinking, so he specially asked the boatman to prepare four dishes and warm a jin of wine to send to the leading boat.
